Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 2:

(p-٣) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-A'raf

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So let there be no constriction in your breast concerning it﴾ — the verse.

Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Suddi said: "Haraj" means doubt, i.e., let there be no doubt in your breast that this Qur'an is the truth. According to this view, the verse is like:

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters﴾ [al-Baqarah: 147],

• and His saying: ﴿The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 60],

• and His saying: ﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you, ask those who recite the Scripture before you. The truth has certainly come to you from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters﴾ [Yunus: 94].

Al-mumtari is the doubter, because it is a form of al-mirya, which is doubt. According to this view, the address is to the Prophet ﷺ.

The intended meaning is the prohibition of others from doubting the Qur'an, as in the words of the rajiz (poet):

"It is you I mean, so listen, O neighbour."

And:

• like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not obey from among them one who is sinful or ungrateful﴾ [al-Insan: 24],

• and His saying: ﴿If you should associate others with Allah, your deeds would surely be nullified﴾ [al-Zumar: 65],

• and His saying: ﴿And if you were to follow their desires...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 120 and 145] and [al-Ra'd: 137].

It is known that the Prophet ﷺ would never do any of that, but Allah addresses him so that the address is directed to others within his own address ﷺ.

The majority of scholars hold that the meaning of "haraj" in the verse is constriction (dhiq). That is: let there be no constriction in your breast regarding conveying what you have been commanded, because of the intensity of their denial of you. Bearing the enmity of the disbelievers and facing their violence are things that constrict the breast, and likewise their denial of him ﷺ despite the clarity of his truthfulness through the dazzling miracles is something that constricts the breast. The Prophet ﷺ said: "They would crush my head and leave it like a loaf of bread," narrated by Muslim. "Al-thalgh" is crushing; it has been said it is striking the soft with the hard until it is smashed. This violence is among the things that constrict the breast.

This last interpretation is supported by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Perhaps you would leave out some of what is revealed to you, and your breast would be constricted by it﴾ [Hud: 12]; and His saying: ﴿We know that your breast is constricted by what they say﴾ [al-Hijr: 97]; and His saying: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over them, if they do not believe in this message﴾ [al-Kahf: 6]; and His saying: ﴿Perhaps you would destroy yourself that they will not be believers﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 3].

The last interpretation is also confirmed by the fact that "haraj" in the Arabic language means constriction. This is well known in their speech, and from it is His saying: ﴿There is no blame on the blind man﴾ [al-Nur: 61]; His saying: ﴿And He has not placed upon you any hardship in religion﴾ [al-Hajj: 78]; and His saying: ﴿He makes his breast tight and constricted﴾ [al-An'am: 125], meaning: extremely constricted. And from it is the saying of Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah, or Jamil: [al-Kamil]

"So I went out, fearing her oath, and she smiled, and I knew that her oath was not a hardship (lam tuhraj)."

And the saying of al-'Arji [al-Sari']:

"Turn towards us, O mistress of the howdah, for if you do not, you will be constrained (tahruj)."

The meaning of "ihraj" in the two verses is: putting into constriction, in the sense of constriction as we have mentioned.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That you may warn thereby, and as a reminder for the believers﴾.

Here He did not specify the object of "li-tunthira" (that you may warn), but He specified it in other places, such as:

• His saying: ﴿And warn thereby a stubborn people﴾ [Maryam: 97],

• and His saying: ﴿That you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned﴾ [Ya-Sin: 6], and other verses. Likewise He specified the second object of warning in other verses, such as:

• His saying: ﴿To warn of severe punishment from Him﴾ [al-Kahf: 2],

• and His saying: ﴿So I have warned you of a Fire that blazes﴾ [al-Layl: 14],

• and His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment﴾ [al-Naba': 40],

and other verses.

In this noble verse He combined warning and reminder in His saying: ﴿That you may warn thereby, and as a reminder for the believers﴾ [al-A'raf: 2]. So the warning is for the disbelievers and the reminder is for the believers. This is supported by His saying: ﴿So We have made it easy in your tongue only that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous and warn thereby a stubborn people﴾ [Maryam: 97]; His saying: ﴿And remind, for indeed the reminder benefits the believers﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 55]; and His saying: ﴿So remind by the Qur'an whoever fears My warning﴾ [Qaf: 45].

(p-٥) What we have mentioned, that the warning is for the disbelievers and the reminder is for the believers, is not contradicted by His saying: ﴿You can only warn one who follows the reminder and fears the Most Merciful unseen. So give him good tidings of forgiveness and a noble reward﴾ [Ya-Sin: 11], in which He restricted warning to them alone, excluding others. This is because, since benefit from the warning is restricted to them, the warning becomes as if restricted to them, for what has no benefit in it is like nonexistence.

Among the methods of the Arabic language is expressing little benefit as if it were nothing.

The summary of the investigation of this topic is that warning in the Qur'an is used in two senses:

The first: general, for all people, as in His saying: ﴿O you who are wrapped up! Arise and warn﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 1-2], and His saying: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [al-Furqan: 1].

This general warning is the one restricted to believers in a relative restriction in His saying: ﴿You can only warn one who follows the reminder﴾ — the verse; because they are the ones who benefit from it, not others.

The second: a warning specific to the disbelievers, because they are the ones who fall into what they are warned of, of punishment and torment. This is what is mentioned in the Qur'an explicitly as specific to the disbelievers and not the believers, as in His saying: ﴿to give good tidings to the righteous and warn a stubborn people﴾, and His saying here: ﴿That you may warn thereby, and as a reminder for the believers﴾. End quote.

Warning (al-indhar) in the Arabic language is informing accompanied by a threat. Thus every warning is an informing, but not every informing is a warning.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 4:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿How many a city have We destroyed, and Our punishment came upon it by night, or while they were taking their midday rest.﴾ In this noble verse, God Most High warned the disbelievers who denied him ﷺ, that He had destroyed many cities because of their denial of the messengers. Among them were those He destroyed ﴿by night﴾, that is, at night, and among them were those He destroyed while they were ﴿taking their midday rest﴾, that is, during their qaylula (the midday rest), and the qaylula is resting in the middle of the day. The meaning is: beware of denying My Messenger (ﷺ), lest there descend upon you the like of what I sent down upon them. He clarified this meaning in other verses,

- such as His saying: ﴿And messengers before you were mocked, but those who mocked them were encompassed by what they used to mock.﴾ [al-An'am: 10],

- and His saying: ﴿And how many a city did We destroy while it was wrongdoing, so it lies in ruins over its roofs, and [many] a well abandoned and a lofty palace.﴾ [al-Hajj: 45],

- and His saying: ﴿And how many a city did We destroy which exulted in its livelihood. Those are their dwellings, not inhabited after them except for a little. And We were the inheritors.﴾ [al-Qasas: 58],

and His saying: ﴿Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? Allah destroyed them, and for the disbelievers is the like thereof.﴾ Then He explained that He (p-6) intends by this to threaten them, in His saying: ﴿And for the disbelievers is the like thereof﴾, and other verses besides these.

God Most High has threatened the people of the cities that His punishment would come upon them at night while they sleep, or in the forenoon while they are at play, in His saying: ﴿Do the people of the cities feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them by night while they are sleeping?﴾ ﴿Or do the people of the cities feel secure that Our punishment will not come upon them in the forenoon while they are playing?﴾ [al-A'raf: 97, 98]. He also threatened their likes among those who plotted evil deeds, in His saying: ﴿Do those who plot evil deeds feel secure that Allah will not cause the earth to swallow them, or that the punishment will not come upon them from where they do not perceive?﴾ ﴿Or that He will not seize them in their going back and forth, so they cannot escape?﴾ ﴿Or that He will not seize them through gradual wasting? For indeed your Lord is Kind and Merciful.﴾ [al-Nahl: 45, 46, 47].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 5:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So their cry was not but that they said, "Indeed, we were wrongdoers."﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, makes clear that those many towns which He destroyed, whether during the night or during the midday rest, had no cry other than their acknowledgment that they had been wrongdoers.

He clarified this meaning in His saying: ﴿And how many a town did We destroy that had been wrongdoing, and We produced after them another people. And when they perceived Our might, there they were fleeing from it. "Do not flee, but return to that in which you were given luxury and to your dwellings that you may be questioned." They said, "Woe to us! Indeed, we have been wrongdoers." And that claim of theirs did not cease until We made them as cut-down crops, extinguished.﴾ [al-Anbiya: 11-15].

Ibn Jarir (may Allah have mercy on him) said: In this verse there is clear evidence for the soundness of what has been transmitted from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "No people perish until they have given an excuse from themselves." Ibn Humayd narrated this to us: Jarir narrated to us from Abu Sinan, from Abd al-Malik ibn Maysarah al-Zarrad, who said: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No people perish until they have given an excuse from themselves." He said: I said to Abdullah, "How is that?" He said: Then he recited this verse: ﴿So their cry was not but that they said, "Indeed, we were wrongdoers."﴾ [al-A'raf: 5].

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers﴾.

He does not specify here what the messengers will be asked about, nor what those to whom they were sent will be asked about.

He explains in other places that He will question the messengers about what their nations responded to them with, and He will question the nations about what they responded to their messengers with.

In the first case He said: ﴿On the Day when Allah will gather the messengers and say, "What was your response?"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 109].

(p-7) In the second case He said: ﴿And on the Day He calls to them and says, "What was your response to the messengers?"﴾ [al-Qasas: 65].

In another place He explains that He will question all creation about what they used to do, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿By your Lord, We will surely question them all, about what they used to do﴾ [al-Hijr: 92–93].

Here there is a well-known difficulty: He said here, ﴿So We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers﴾ [al-A'raf: 6]. He also said, ﴿By your Lord, We will surely question them all, about what they used to do﴾, and said, ﴿And stop them, for they are to be questioned﴾ [al-Saffat: 24]. This is clear in affirming the questioning of everyone on the Day of Resurrection, yet He said, ﴿And the guilty will not be asked about their sins﴾ [al-Qasas: 78], and He said, ﴿On that Day, neither man nor jinn will be asked about his sin﴾ [al-Rahman: 39].

We have already explained how to reconcile the verses mentioned in our book (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab) (Dispelling the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book), and we will add further clarification here, if Allah the Exalted wills.

Know first that the questioning that is negated in the mentioned verses is more specific than the questioning that is affirmed in them, because the negated questioning is restricted to being a questioning about particular sins. He said, ﴿And the guilty will not be asked about their sins﴾ [al-Qasas: 78], so He specified it as being about sins. He said, ﴿On that Day, neither man nor jinn will be asked about his sin﴾, so He specified it in the same way. From this it becomes clear that the questioning of the messengers and of the buried infant, for example, is not about a sin they committed, so there is no obstacle to its occurrence, because what is negated is specifically questioning about a sin. This is further clarified by His saying, ﴿That He may question the truthful about their truthfulness﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 119], and by His saying after His questioning of Jesus, mentioned in His saying, ﴿Did you say to the people, "Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 116], and ﴿Allah said, "This is a Day when the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 119]. The questioning about sins that is negated in the verses is meant as questioning for information and inquiry, because His knowledge, may He be majestic and exalted, encompasses everything. The negation of this type of questioning does not contradict the affirmation of another type of it, which is the questioning of rebuke and reproach, because that is a kind of punishment. What supports this is that Allah's questioning of the disbelievers throughout the Qur'an is a rebuke and reproach, as in His saying, ﴿And stop them, for they are to be questioned. What is wrong with you that you do not help one another?﴾ [al-Saffat: 24–25].

And His saying, ﴿Is this magic, or is it that you do not see?﴾ [al-Tur: 15], and other verses besides these. The remaining aspects of reconciliation are explained in our aforementioned book, and knowledge is with Allah, may He be exalted.

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

(p-288) In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

Surah al-A'raf.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent, and We will surely question the messengers﴾.

This noble verse indicates that Allah will question all people on the Day of Resurrection. Its parallels are His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿By your Lord, We will surely question them all, about what they used to do﴾ [al-Hijr: 92–93], His saying: ﴿And stop them, for they are to be questioned﴾ [al-Saffat: 24], and His saying: ﴿And on the Day He calls to them and says, "What was your response to the messengers?"﴾ [al-Qasas: 65].

Other verses have come that indicate the opposite, such as His saying: ﴿On that Day, neither man nor jinn will be asked about his sin﴾ [al-Rahman: 39], and His saying: ﴿And the guilty will not be asked about their sins﴾ [al-Qasas: 78].

The answer to this is in three aspects:

The first, which is the strongest of them in terms of the Qur'an's indication of it, is that questioning is of two kinds:

Questioning of rebuke and reproach, whose particle is usually "why" (lima), and questioning of inquiry and information, whose particle is usually "did" (hal). The affirmed questioning is the questioning of rebuke and reproach, and the negated questioning is the questioning of inquiry and information. The evidence from the Qur'an for this is that His questioning of them, as stated throughout it, is rebuke and reproach, as in His saying: ﴿And stop them, for they are to be questioned. What is wrong with you that you do not help one another?﴾ [al-Saffat: 24–25], and His saying: ﴿Is this magic, or is it that you do not see?﴾ [al-Tur: 15], ﴿Did there not come to you messengers from among you?﴾ [al-Zumar: 71], and as in His saying: ﴿Did there not come to you a warner?﴾ [al-Mulk: 8], and other verses besides these.

As for Allah's questioning of the messengers: ﴿What was your response?﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 109], it is for rebuking those who denied them, like the questioning of the buried infant: ﴿For what sin was she killed?﴾ [al-Takwir: 9], for rebuking her killer.

(p-289) The second aspect: On the Day of Resurrection there are multiple standing places. In some of them they will be questioned, and in some of them they will not be questioned.

The third aspect is what al-Halimi mentioned, that the affirmation of questioning is to be understood as questioning about monotheism and the affirmation of the messengers, and the negation of questioning is to be understood as what the acknowledgment of prophethood entails of the laws of religion and its branches. What supports this is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then He will say, "What was your response to the messengers?"﴾ [al-Qasas: 65], and knowledge is with Allah, may He be exalted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 7:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We will surely relate to them with knowledge, and We were not absent.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, makes clear that on the Day of Resurrection He will relate to His servants what they used to do in the world, and He informs them that He, majestic and exalted, was not absent from what they did at the time of their doing it in the abode of this world. Rather, He is the Watchful, the Witness over all creation, whose knowledge encompasses everything they did, small and great, significant and insignificant. He has made this meaning clear in many verses:

• Such as His saying: ﴿There is not a secret conversation among three but that He is their fourth, nor among five but that He is their sixth, nor less than that nor more but that He is with them wherever they are. Then He will inform them of what they did on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 7]

• And His saying: ﴿He knows what enters into the earth and what emerges from it, and what descends from the sky and what ascends therein. And He is with you wherever you are.﴾ [al-Hadid: 4]

• And His saying: ﴿And you are not engaged in any matter, nor recite from it any Qur'an, nor do you do any deed, except that We are witnesses over you when you are involved in it. And not absent from your Lord is any [part] of an atom's weight within the earth or within the heaven or [anything] smaller than that or greater, but it is in a clear register.﴾ [Yunus: 61]

A Warning (Tanbih)

In this noble verse there is a clear refutation of the Mu'tazilah, who deny the attributes of meaning (sifat al-ma'ani), and who say that He, exalted is He, is Knowing by His essence, not by an attribute subsisting in His essence which is knowledge. The same applies to their saying: Powerful, Willing, Living, Hearing, Seeing, Speaking. Here He affirmed for Himself the attribute of knowledge by His saying: ﴿So We will surely relate to them with knowledge﴾ [al-A'raf: 7]. A parallel to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He has sent it down with His knowledge﴾ [an-Nisa': 166]. These are clear Qur'anic proofs against the invalidity of their doctrine, which no rational person doubts is invalid and self-contradictory.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 8:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the weighing on that Day is the truth﴾. In this noble verse, He, exalted is He, explains that His weighing of deeds on the Day of Resurrection is true, meaning there is no injustice in it and no wrongdoing. Thus, no evil deeds are increased for the wrongdoer, and no good deeds are decreased for the doer of good.

He clarified this meaning in other places, such as His saying: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged in anything. And even if it is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as Reckoners﴾ [al-Anbiya' 47], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong [even] the weight of an atom. And if it is a good deed, He multiplies it﴾ [an-Nisa' 40], and others besides these verses.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So whoever's scales are heavy, those are the successful﴾ ﴿And whoever's scales are light, those are the ones who have lost themselves, for what they used to deny of Our verses they were doing wrong﴾.

In this noble verse, He, exalted is He, explains that whoever's scales are heavy will be successful, and whoever's scales are light will be losers because of their wrongdoing. He did not detail the success (falah) and the loss (khusran) here.

Yet in some other places there is what indicates that what is meant by success here is that he is in a pleasant life in Paradise, and what is meant by loss here is that he is in the abyss of the Fire. This is in His saying: ﴿As for one whose scales are heavy, he will be in a pleasant life. And as for one whose scales are light, his refuge will be an abyss. And what can make you know what that is? It is a fierce Fire﴾ [al-Qari'ah 6–11].

He also explained the loss of one whose scales are light in His saying: ﴿And whoever's scales are light, those are the ones who have lost themselves, in Hell they will abide forever. The Fire will burn their faces, and they therein will be grimacing﴾ [al-Mu'minun 103–104], and others besides these verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 10:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have made for you therein means of living (ma'ayish)﴾. Here He did not explain the manner of these means of living which He placed for us on the earth, but He explained that in other places, such as His saying: ﴿So let man look at his food﴾ ﴿That We poured down water in torrents﴾ ﴿Then We broke open the earth, splitting it open﴾ ﴿And caused to grow therein grain﴾ ﴿And grapes and herbage﴾ ﴿And olives and palm trees﴾ ﴿And gardens of dense trees﴾ ﴿And fruits and pasture﴾ ﴿As provision for you and for your cattle﴾ [Abasa: 24-32].

And His saying: ﴿Do they not see that We drive the water to the barren land and thereby bring out crops from which their cattle and they themselves eat? Will they not then see?﴾ [As-Sajdah: 27], and His saying: ﴿And He sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth thereby pairs of various kinds of plants. Eat and graze your cattle. The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿He said, "What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?"﴾.

Some scholars said: its meaning is, "What prevented you from prostrating?" and "lā" (not) is redundant (ṣila). (p-10) The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿He said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."﴾ In this noble verse, it is mentioned that Iblis, may Allah curse him, was created from fire. On the view that Iblis is the jinn who is the father of the jinn, other descriptions of the fire from which he was created are mentioned in other places. Among them, it is the "fire of samūm" (scorching wind), as in His words: ﴿And the jinn We had created before from the fire of samūm﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 27]. Among them, it is specifically the *mārij* (smokeless flame), as in His words: ﴿And He created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire﴾ [al-Raḥmān: 15]. The *mārij* is more specific than fire in general, because it is the flame that has no smoke in it.

It was called the "fire of samūm" because it penetrates the pores of the body due to the intensity of its heat. In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, from ʿĀ'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ): "The angels were created from light, the jinn were created from a smokeless flame of fire, and Adam was created from what has been described to you." It was also narrated from her by Imam Aḥmad.

The author said in (*Daf' Īhām al-Iḍṭirāb 'an Āyāt al-Kitāb*):

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿He said, "What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?"﴾.

In this verse there is an apparent difficulty between His words "mana'aka" (prevented you) together with the negating "lā" (not), because what would seem appropriate in the outward sense to His words "mana'aka," according to what comes to the listener's mind and not what is in reality, is the omission of "lā," so that it would say, "mā mana'aka an tasjuda" (what prevented you from prostrating) instead of "allā tasjuda" (that you not prostrate). This has been answered with several answers. Among the closest of them is what Ibn Jarir chose in his tafsir (exegesis), which is that the sentence contains an omission that the context indicates.

Accordingly, the meaning is: "What prevented you from prostrating, so that you were compelled not to prostrate when I commanded you?" This is what Ibn Jarir chose, and Ibn Kathir said: it is good and strong.

Among their answers is that "lā" is redundant (ṣila), and the words of Allah the Exalted in Surah Ṣād support this: ﴿What prevented you from prostrating to what I created?﴾ [38:75]. We have promised earlier that, if Allah wills, we will explain the view on the addition of "lā," with its Arabic evidence, in combining His words: ﴿I do not swear by this city﴾ [90:1] with His words: ﴿and this secure city﴾ [al-Tīn: 3].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 13:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "Then descend from it, for it is not for you to be arrogant therein, so get out; indeed, you are of the debased."﴾ [Al-A'raf: 13].

In this noble verse, Allah the Exalted explains that He dealt with the accursed Iblis in a manner opposite to his intention. His intention was self-magnification and arrogance, so Allah expelled him, humbled, abased and disgraced, characterized by the very opposite of the height and greatness he had sought. This is in His saying: ﴿So get out; indeed, you are of the debased﴾ [Al-A'raf: 13]. Al-saghar (debasement) is the most extreme humiliation and abasement.

• And His saying: ﴿Get out of it, reproached and expelled﴾ [Al-A'raf: 18], and similar verses. It is understood from the verse that the arrogant one does not attain the greatness and elevation he desires; rather, the opposite of that is what befalls him. Allah the Exalted stated this meaning explicitly in His saying: ﴿There is nothing in their breasts but pride, which they will never attain﴾ [Ghafir: 56]. In other places He explained many of the evil consequences that arise from arrogance, may Allah protect us and the Muslims from it. Among these is that it is a cause of turning its possessor away from understanding the signs of Allah and being guided by them, as in His saying: ﴿I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant on earth without right﴾ [Al-A'raf: 146], and so on. Among them also is that it is one of the causes of dwelling in the Fire, as in His saying: ﴿Is there not in Hell an abode for the arrogant?﴾ [Az-Zumar: 60].

• And His saying: ﴿Indeed, they, when it was said to them, "There is no deity except Allah," would become arrogant﴾ [As-Saffat: 35]. Among them also is that Allah the Exalted does not love its possessor, as in His saying: ﴿Surely Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Indeed, He does not love the arrogant﴾ [An-Nahl: 23]. Among them also is that Musa sought refuge from one characterized by it, and one seeks refuge only from what is evil, as in His saying: ﴿And Musa said, "Indeed, I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning"﴾ [Ghafir: 27].

And beyond that from its (p-11) other evil results and its grave consequences. And it is understood from the inverse implication (mafhum al-mukhalafa) of the verse that the one who is humble before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is raised up by Allah.

Allah the Exalted has also indicated the standing of those who are humble before Him in other places, such as His saying: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk on the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace"﴾ [Al-Furqan: 63], and His saying: ﴿That is the Last Abode; We assign it to those who do not desire superiority on earth or corruption, and the best outcome is for the righteous﴾ [Al-Qasas: 83]. It is authentically reported from him (ﷺ) that he said: "It has been revealed to me that you should be humble, so that no one boasts over another, and no one oppresses another." The poet said: [Al-Tawil]

Be humble, and you will be like the full moon, whose face you see reflected on the surfaces of water, while it is lofty.

And do not be like the smoke, which rises by itself to the surfaces of the sky, while it is base.

And Abu al-Tayyib al-Mutanabbi said: [Al-Wafir]

Were it not that only one of station rises, the army would be exalted and the dust would sink down.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 14:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said: "Reprieve me until the day they are raised."﴾ ﴿He said: "Indeed, you are among those reprieved."﴾

He does not specify here, in Surat al-A'raf, the term up to which He granted him reprieve. He has mentioned it in al-Hijr and Sad, clarifying that the end of that reprieve is the day of the appointed time (yawm al-waqt al-ma'lum).

This is based on His saying, in Surat al-Hijr and Sad: ﴿So indeed you are among those reprieved﴾ ﴿until the day of the appointed time﴾ [15:37-38; 38:80-81]. Thus Satan requested reprieve until the day of resurrection, and Allah granted him reprieve until the day of the appointed time.

Most of the scholars say: what is meant by it is the time of the first blast (al-nafkha al-ula), and knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

The Exalted said: ﴿And You will not find most of them grateful.﴾ This that Iblis mentioned, that he would bring the children of Adam into it, he said out of assumption on his part that they would obey him in what he calls them to, until he destroys them. And the Exalted has made clear in Surah "Saba" that his assumption was true regarding them, by His saying: ﴿And Iblis had already confirmed his assumption about them, so they followed him﴾ [Saba' 34:20], as the indication to it has already passed.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 18:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "Get out of it, reviled and expelled. Whoever follows you among them – I will surely fill Hell with you all."﴾ [Sad: 84, 85].

In this noble verse He makes clear that He said to Iblis: "Get out of it, being reviled and expelled." Al-mad'um (reviled) means blamed or detested, and al-mad'ur (expelled) means distanced from mercy, driven away. He also threatened him that He would fill Jahannam (Hell) with him. He clarified this meaning in other verses,

such as His statement, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "The truth is so, and I say the truth: I will surely fill Hell with you and with whoever follows you among them, all together."﴾ [Sad: 84, 85];

and His statement: ﴿He said, "Go, and whoever follows you among them – indeed, Hell is your recompense, a full recompense. And incite whomever you can among them with your voice, and attack them with your horses and your foot soldiers, and share with them in wealth and children, and make promises to them." And Satan does not promise them except delusion.﴾ [al-Isra': 63, 64];

and His statement: ﴿So they will be thrown into it, they and the deviators, and the soldiers of Iblis, all together.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 94, 95]

and other verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 27:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from the Garden﴾.

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, warns the children of Adam that Satan may tempt them as he tempted their parents. In another place He stated explicitly that He had warned Adam of the scheming of Iblis before he fell into what he fell into, and that this warning did not save him from his enemy. This is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We said, "O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so let him not remove you both from the Garden, for then you would be distressed"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 117].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 28:

The words of His, the Exalted: ﴿And when they commit an immorality, they say, "We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to do it."﴾ — the verse.

In this noble verse, He, the Exalted, mentions that when the disbelievers commit an immorality, they take as evidence that it is true and correct the fact that they found their fathers doing it, and that they did not do it except because it is correct and right guidance.

And He clarifies in another place that this occurs among all nations, namely His words, the Exalted: ﴿And thus We did not send before you a warner into any town but its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and indeed we are following in their footsteps."﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 23].

Allah refuted this blind imitation (taqlid) in many verses,

• such as His saying: ﴿Even though their fathers understood nothing and were not guided?﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 170],

• and His saying: ﴿Even though their fathers knew nothing and were not guided?﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 104],

• and His saying: ﴿[The warner] said, "Even if I brought you better guidance than that which you found your fathers upon?"﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 24],

• and His saying: ﴿Indeed, they found their fathers astray. So they were rushing to follow in their footsteps.﴾ [As-Saffat: 69-70]

and other verses besides these.

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

The words of His, the Exalted: ﴿Say, "Indeed, Allah does not order immorality."﴾

This noble verse may give rise to the apparent impression of contradicting what another verse apparently indicates, namely His words, the Exalted: ﴿And when We intend to destroy a town, We command its affluent ones, and they defiantly commit wickedness therein﴾ — the verse [Al-Isra': 16].

The answer to this is in three respects:

The first, and the most apparent of them: that the meaning of His words ﴿We command its affluent ones﴾ is, i.e., to obey Allah and affirm the messengers, ﴿and they defiantly commit wickedness﴾, i.e., by denying the messengers and disobeying Allah, the Exalted. So there is no difficulty in the verse at all.

(p-290) The second: that the command in His words ﴿We command its affluent ones﴾ is a cosmic, predestined command, not a legislative command; i.e., We decreed wickedness upon them by Our will. The cosmic predestined command is like His words, the Exalted: ﴿Be apes, despised﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 65], and ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin: 82]. The command in His words ﴿Say, "Indeed, Allah does not order immorality"﴾ is a legislative, religious command. Thus it is evident that the negated command is other than the affirmed command.

The third: that the meaning of ﴿We command its affluent ones﴾ is: i.e., We multiplied them until they became insolent toward the blessing, ﴿and they defiantly commit wickedness﴾. This meaning is supported by the hadith which Imam Ahmad narrated, raised (to the Prophet ﷺ), from the hadith of Suwayd ibn Hubayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): "The best wealth of a man is a fertile mare or a pollinated palm row (sikkah ma'burah)." Here His words "ma'murah" mean abundant in offspring, and this is the point of evidence.

Al-Shinqiti's commentary on Surah 7, verse 29:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿As He originated you, you will return.﴾

In this noble verse, the scholars have two interpretations.

The first: the meaning of ﴿As He originated you, you will return﴾ is: just as there has already preceded in Allah's knowledge concerning you happiness or wretchedness, so you will return to Him. Whoever has been preceded by knowledge that he is blessed attains to happiness, and whoever has been preceded by knowledge that he is wretched attains to wretchedness. The evidence for this interpretation is His saying after it: ﴿A group He guided, and a group deserved misguidance﴾ [al-A'raf: 30]. This is clear, as you see. Among the verses that also indicate it is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is He who created you, so among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾ [at-Taghabun: 2], and His saying: ﴿And for that He created them﴾ [Hud: 119], meaning: for that difference, between a wretched one and a blessed one, He created them.

The second interpretation: the meaning of His saying: ﴿As He originated you, you will return﴾ [al-A'raf: 29] is: just as He created you at first, when you were nothing, He will restore you a second time and raise you from your graves alive after you have died and become decayed bones. The verses indicating this interpretation are very numerous, such as:

• His saying: ﴿As We originated the first creation, We will repeat it; a promise upon Us﴾ [al-Anbiya': 104], the verse.

• His saying: ﴿And it is He who begins the creation and then repeats it﴾ [ar-Rum: 27], the verse.

• His saying: ﴿Say: He will give them life who produced them the first time﴾ [Ya-Sin: 79], the verse.

• His saying: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then indeed We created you from dust﴾ [al-Hajj: 5].

And other verses besides these.

We have already mentioned, in the introduction to this blessed book, that a verse may have two interpretations, each of which is true and is supported by the Qur'an. So we mention all of them, since all of it is true, and knowledge is with Allah, may He be exalted.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 30:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, they have taken the devils as allies instead of Allah, and they think that they are guided.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah the Exalted explains that the disbelievers have taken the devils (shayatin) as allies (awliya') instead of Allah. Among this alliance is their obedience to them in what contradicts what Allah the Exalted has legislated. Yet, despite this, they consider themselves to be upon guidance.

He explains in another place that whoever is like this is the greatest loser in deeds, and we seek refuge in Allah the Exalted. This is His saying, majestic and exalted is He: ﴿Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in deeds? Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world while they think they are doing good work.﴾ [al-Kahf: 103, 104].

Note (tanbih)

These Qur'anic texts indicate that the disbeliever is not benefited by his assumption that he is upon guidance, because the proofs which the messengers brought did not leave any ambiguity or doubt concerning the truth. However, the disbeliever, due to the intensity of his zealotry for disbelief, hardly reflects upon the proofs, which are like the sun at the height of midday, out of obstinacy in falsehood and stubbornness (p-14). Therefore he is not excused. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 32:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has brought forth for His servants, and the good things of provision?﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, commanded His Prophet ﷺ to ask, in a manner of denunciation: who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has brought forth for His servants, such as clothing during the circumambulation (tawaf), and the good things of provision such as the livestock and tilth which the disbelievers had forbidden, and such as the meat and fat which some of the Arabs in the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance) forbade during the Hajj.

He also declared in other places that whoever says this about Allah is a fabricator against Him, exalted and high, such as His saying:

• ﴿And do not say, concerning what your tongues describe falsely, "This is lawful and this is unlawful," to invent falsehood against Allah. Indeed, those who invent falsehood against Allah will not succeed.﴾ [al-Nahl: 116],

• And His saying: ﴿They have certainly lost who have killed their children in foolishness without knowledge and have forbidden what Allah has provided for them, inventing lies against Allah. They have certainly gone astray and were not guided.﴾ [al-An'am: 140],

• And His saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered what Allah has sent down to you of provision, and you made from it [some] unlawful and [some] lawful? Say: Has Allah permitted you, or do you invent [lies] against Allah?﴾ [Yunus: 59]. And their demand in another place was a demand of challenge: that they bring the witnesses who would testify for them that Allah had forbidden this. He forbade His Prophet ﷺ, if false witnesses testified for them, to testify along with them, and this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Bring your witnesses who testify that Allah has forbidden this. But if they testify, do not testify with them.﴾ [al-An'am: 150] 30

And to other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 38:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Until, when they have all overtaken one another therein, the last of them will say of the first of them, "Our Lord, these are the ones who misled us, so give them a double punishment from the Fire."﴾

He did not specify here the cause that enabled them to mislead others. However, He explained in another place that the cause which enabled them to do so was that they were their leaders (sādah) and great ones (kubarā'), and it is known that followers obey great leaders in what they command them. This is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they will say, "Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our leaders and our great ones, and they led us astray from the way." ﴿Our Lord, give them double the punishment⁠—﴾ [al-Ahzab: 67-68], and the verse goes on. He elaborated on this in Surah Saba' with His saying: ﴿And if you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord, [and] they refer back statements to one another. Those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "If not for you, we would have been believers." Those who were arrogant will say to those who were oppressed, "Did we avert you from guidance after it had come to you? Rather, you were criminals." And those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Rather, [it was] scheming by night and day when you were ordering us to disbelieve in Allah and set up rivals to Him."﴾ [Saba': 31-33].

*  *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So give them a double punishment from the Fire.﴾

In this noble verse and its like, Allah, exalted is He, has explained that the followers will ask Allah on the Day of Resurrection to multiply the punishment for the leaders, (p-15) and He has explained in other places that multiplying the punishment for the leaders does not benefit the followers, nor does it lighten their punishment,

• as in His saying: ﴿And it will not benefit you today, since you wronged [yourselves], that you are, in the punishment, sharers [in it].﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 39],

• and His saying here: ﴿He will say, "For each is double, but you do not know."﴾ and the verse goes on [al-A'raf: 38],

• and His saying: ﴿And the first of them will say to the last of them, "You had no superiority over us, so taste the punishment for what you used to earn."﴾ [al-A'raf: 39],

• and His saying: ﴿Those who were arrogant will say, "Indeed, all of us are in it. Indeed, Allah has already judged between the servants."﴾ [Ghafir: 48],

and other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 43:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts, with rivers flowing beneath them.﴾

In this noble verse, He, exalted and majestic, mentions that He removes from the breasts of the people of Paradise the rancor (ghill) and envy (hasad) that existed in the worldly life, and that rivers flow beneath them in Paradise. In another place He mentions that the removal of rancor from their breasts takes place while they are brothers, facing one another on couches, secure from fatigue and from being expelled from Paradise. This is His saying, exalted is He, in surah al-Hijr: ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts, [they being] brothers on couches facing each other.﴾ ﴿No fatigue will touch them therein, nor will they be removed from it.﴾ [15:47-48].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 46:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And between them is a barrier﴾.

In this noble verse, He, may He be exalted, mentions that on the Day of Resurrection there is a barrier (ḥijāb) between the people of Paradise and the people of Hellfire. He does not explain this barrier here, but He explains it in Surat al-Ḥadīd with His saying: ﴿So a wall will be struck between them with a gate; its inner side will have mercy, and its outer side will face torment﴾ [al-Ḥadīd: 13], and so on.

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They will recognize each of them by their marks﴾.

In this noble verse, He, may He be exalted, mentions that the people of the heights (aṣḥāb al-A'rāf) will recognize each of the people of Paradise and the people of Hellfire by their marks (sīmā). He does not explain here the marks of the people of Paradise or the people of Hellfire, but He alludes to them in other places, such as His saying: ﴿On a Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 106].

So the whiteness and beauty of faces are the marks of the people of Paradise, and their blackness, ugliness, and the blueness of the eyes are the marks of the people of Hellfire. As He also said regarding the marks of the people of Paradise: ﴿You will recognize in their faces the radiance of delight﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 24], and He said: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant﴾ [al-Qiyāmah: 22], and He said regarding the marks of the people of Hellfire: ﴿As if their faces were covered with pieces of the night, made dark﴾ [Yūnus: 27], and He said: ﴿And faces that Day will have dust upon them﴾ [ʿAbasa: 40], and He said: ﴿And We will gather the criminals that Day, blue-eyed﴾ [Ṭā-Hā: 102].

**The Qur'anic verse 48:** He, the Exalted, says: ﴿They will say, "Your gathering (of wealth) did not avail you, nor did what you used to be arrogant about."﴾

(p-16) In this noble verse, He, the Exalted, mentions that the people of the Heights said to certain men of the Fire, whom they recognize by their marks: the wealth you used to amass in the world did not benefit you, nor did the multitude of your company and helpers, nor your arrogance in the world.

He explains the reason for this in other passages. It is that on the Day of Resurrection a person will be gathered alone, with no wealth with him, no helper, no servant, and no attendant. His arrogance in the world will be repaid with the punishment of humiliation in the Hereafter, as in His saying: ﴿And you have certainly come to Us alone, as We created you the first time, and you have left behind you what We bestowed upon you﴾ [al-An'am: 94], and His saying: ﴿And We will inherit from him what he says, and he will come to Us alone﴾ [Maryam: 95], and His saying: ﴿And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection, alone﴾, and His saying: ﴿So today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you were arrogant about in the earth without right﴾ [46 \ 20 ...

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 51:

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of this their Day﴾, the verse.

And similar verses:

• such as His saying: ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 67],

• and His saying: ﴿And thus today you are forgotten﴾ [Ta-Ha: 126],

• and His saying: ﴿And it will be said, "Today We will forget you"﴾, the verse [al-Jathiyah: 34]. They do not contradict His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿My Lord neither errs nor forgets﴾ [Ta-Ha: 52], and His saying: ﴿And your Lord was not forgetful﴾ [Maryam: 64];

because the meaning of ﴿So today We will forget them﴾ and what is similar to it is: that is, We will leave them in the punishment, deprived of every good. And Allah, may He be exalted, knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 53:

The Exalted said: ﴿On the Day when its final outcome comes, those who had forgotten it before will say: "The messengers of our Lord had indeed come with the truth. So do we have any intercessors who might intercede for us, or could we be sent back so that we might act differently from what we used to do?"﴾.

In this noble verse, the Exalted explains that the disbelievers, when they witness the reality on the Day of Resurrection, will acknowledge that the messengers came with the truth, and they will wish for one of two things: that intercessors would intercede for them and rescue them, or that they would be returned to the world so that they could believe the messengers and act in a way that pleases Allah. Here He does not state whether anyone will intercede for them, whether they will be returned, what they would do if they were returned, or whether their acknowledgment of the truthfulness of the messengers will benefit them. However, the Exalted has explained all of that in other passages. He explained that no one will intercede for them, by His saying: ﴿So we have no intercessors﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 100], and His saying: ﴿So the intercession of the interceders will not benefit them﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 48],

- and His saying: ﴿And they do not intercede except for those whom He approves﴾ [al-Anbiya': 28], together with His saying: ﴿And He does not approve for His servants disbelief﴾ [al-Zumar: 7],

- and His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is not pleased with the defiant people﴾ [al-Tawbah: 96]. He also explained that they will not be returned, in many passages,

- such as His saying: ﴿If only you could see when the criminals will hang their heads before their Lord, saying, "Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so send us back; we will act righteously; indeed, we are now certain."﴾ ﴿And if We had willed, We would have given every soul its guidance, but the word from Me has come into effect: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and men all together."﴾ [al-Sajdah: 12, 13].

So His saying: ﴿But the word from Me has come into effect: "I will surely fill Hell"﴾, up to the end of the verse, is evidence that the Fire has become obligatory for them, so they will not be returned and will not be excused. And His saying: ﴿They will cry out therein, "Our Lord, bring us out; we will act righteously, not as we used to act." Did We not give you a life long enough for whoever would remember to remember therein, and the warner had come to you?﴾ [Fatir: 37].

Thus He clearly stated that He had cut off their excuse in the world, by granting them a period in which they could remember, and by the warning of the messengers. This is evidence that they will not be returned to the world again. He pointed to this by His saying: ﴿Had you not sworn before that there would be no end for you?﴾ [Ibrahim: 44], as a reply

- to their saying: "Delay us to a near term; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers,"

- and His saying: ﴿That is because when Allah alone was invoked, you disbelieved, and when partners were associated with Him, you believed﴾ [Ghafir: 12], after His saying about them: ﴿So we have acknowledged our sins; is there any way out?﴾ [Ghafir: 11],

- and His saying: ﴿And you will see them presented before it, humbled from abasement, glancing with a furtive look﴾ [al-Shura: 45], after His saying: ﴿And whomever Allah sends astray, for him there is no protector after Him. And you will see the wrongdoers, when they see the punishment, saying: "Is there any way to return?"﴾ [al-Shura: 44],

- and His saying here: ﴿They have lost their souls﴾ [al-A'raf: 53], after His saying: ﴿So do we have any intercessors who might intercede for us, or could we be sent back?﴾.

All of that indicates that they will not be returned to the world, that the punishment is obligatory, and that there is no escape for them from it.

In another place, He explained that if they were returned, they would revert to disbelief and rebellion, by His saying: ﴿And if they were returned, they would certainly return to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-An'am: 28]. In this noble verse there is clear evidence that the Exalted knows the non-existent but possible thing which, in His knowledge, will never come into existence, how it would be if it did exist. Thus the Exalted knows that they will not be returned to the world again, and He knows how that return, which will not happen, would be if it occurred, as He stated in His saying: ﴿And if they were returned, they would certainly return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars﴾. He also knows that the hypocrites who stayed behind from the Battle of Tabuk will not attend it, because He is the one who held them back from it for a wisdom, as He explained by His saying: ﴿But Allah disliked their going forth, so He held them back﴾ [al-Tawbah: 46]. He knows how this going forth, which will not occur, would be if it did occur, as He stated in His saying: ﴿Had they gone out among you, they would not have increased you except in corruption, and they would have hastened between your ranks, seeking to cause you discord﴾ [al-Tawbah: 47]. A similar example is the Exalted's saying: ﴿And even if We had mercy on them and removed what afflicts them of harm, they would persist in their defiance, wandering blindly﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 75], and other verses of this kind.

In other places He explained that their acknowledgment, by their saying: ﴿The messengers of our Lord had indeed come with the truth﴾, will not benefit them, as the Exalted said: ﴿So they acknowledged their sin, so away with the companions of the Blaze﴾ [al-Mulk: 11], and His saying: ﴿They will say, "Yes, but the word of punishment has come into effect against the disbelievers"﴾ [al-Zumar: 71], and similar verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 54 (part 1 of 4):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾.
He did not detail that here, but He detailed it in the surah "Fussilat" with His saying: ﴿Say, "Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days and attribute to Him equals? That is the Lord of the worlds."﴾ (p-18) ﴿And He placed within it firm mountains from above it, and blessed it, and measured therein its sustenance in four days, equal for those who ask.﴾ ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, "Come [into being], willingly or by compulsion." They said, "We come willingly."﴾ ﴿So He completed them as seven heavens in two days and inspired in each heaven its command.﴾ [Fussilat: 9–12].
* *
His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then He established Himself above the Throne; He causes the night to cover the day﴾, and so on.
This noble verse and its like among the verses of the Attributes, such as His saying: ﴿The Hand of Allah is above their hands﴾ [al-Fath: 10], and similar, have been problematic for many people, and by reason of it an uncountable multitude has gone astray. Some people went to ta'til (denial of the attributes), and some went to tashbih (likening Allah to creation). Glorified and exalted is He, far above all of that with great exaltedness. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has clarified this in the utmost clarity and left in it no ambiguity or problem whatsoever. The summary of the verification of this is that He, Mighty and Majestic, made clear that the truth in the verses of the Attributes is composed of two matters:
The first: the declaring Allah, Mighty and Majestic, free of resembling created things in their attributes, glorified and exalted is He with great exaltedness above that.
The second: belief in everything with which Allah described Himself in His Book, or which His Messenger ﷺ described Him with; for none is more knowledgeable about Allah than Allah Himself: ﴿Are you more knowing or is Allah?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 140]. Nor is anyone more knowledgeable about Allah, after Allah, than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, of whom He said: ﴿Nor does he speak from desire. It is not but a revelation revealed﴾ [an-Najm: 3–4]. So whoever denies of Allah an attribute which He affirmed for Himself in His Mighty Book, or which His Messenger ﷺ affirmed for Him, claiming that this attribute necessarily entails what is not befitting for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made himself more knowledgeable than Allah and His Messenger regarding what is befitting for Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Glory be to You, this is a tremendous slander.
Whoever believes that the description of Allah resembles the attributes of creation is a mushabbih (anthropomorphist), a heretic, astray. And whoever affirms for Allah what He affirmed for Himself or what His Messenger ﷺ affirmed for Him, together with declaring Him, Mighty and Majestic, free of resembling creation, is a believer combining belief in the attributes of perfection and majesty with declaring Him free of resembling creation, safe from the pitfall of tashbih and ta'til. The verse by which Allah clarified this is His saying: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [ash-Shura: 11]. He negated from Himself, Mighty and Majestic, likeness to created things by His saying: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾, and affirmed for Himself the attributes of perfection and majesty by His saying: ﴿and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾. So in this noble verse He explicitly negated likeness while affirming the attributes of perfection and majesty.
It appears that the secret in His expressing it with His saying: ﴿and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾, rather than saying, for example, (p-19) "and He is the Most High, the Mighty," or other comprehensive attributes, is that hearing and sight are attributes shared by all animals. So He showed that Allah is characterized by them, but His description by them is on the basis of negating likeness between His description, exalted is He, and the attributes of His creation. Therefore it came with His saying: ﴿and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ after His saying: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾. So in this noble verse there is a clarification of the truth in the verses of the Attributes, with no ambiguity or doubt whatsoever. We will, if Allah wills, clarify this matter in full clarity to the best of our capacity; and with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is success.
* *
Know first: the mutakallimun (theologians) divided His attributes, Mighty and Majestic, into six categories:
Essential attribute (sifah nafsiyyah), negative attribute (sifah salbiyyah), attribute of meaning (sifat al-ma'ani), attribute of state (sifah ma'nawiyyah), active attribute (sifah fi'liyyah), and comprehensive attribute (sifah jami'ah). The relational attribute (sifah idafiyyah) overlaps with the active attribute, because every active attribute derived from a transitive root that takes an object, such as creating, giving life, and causing death, is a relational attribute. But not every relational attribute is an active attribute, so between them there is a general and specific relation from one aspect: they coincide in such things as creating, giving life, and causing death; the active attribute stands alone in such things as istiwa' (establishing over the Throne), and the relational attribute stands alone in such things as His being existent before everything and above everything, because priority (qabliyyah) and being above (fawqiyyah) are relational attributes and are not attributes of acts. And it is not hidden from a scholar of the theological and logical sciences that applying the term "essential" to any of His attributes, Mighty and Majestic, is impermissible, and that in it there is of audacity toward Allah, Mighty and Majestic, what Allah alone knows. Even if their intention by "essential" regarding Allah was existence only, which is correct, the application that causes a misapprehension regarding Him, exalted is He, is impermissible, even if the meaning intended by it is correct. For the essential attribute in terminology is only a genus (jins) or a differentia (fasl). The genus is like animal in relation to human, and the differentia is like rational speech in relation to human. It is not hidden that the genus in terminology is a common quality shared among individuals of differing realities, like animal in relation to human, horse and donkey; and the differentia is an essential attribute of some individuals of the genus by which it is distinguished from other individuals sharing the genus with it, like rational speech in relation to human, for it is his essential attribute which separates him from the horse, for example, which shares with him in substantiality, corporeality, growth, and sensation. Describing Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with something meant by these terminological senses that I have made clear to you is among the greatest audacities against Allah, exalted, as you see; because He, Mighty and Majestic, is one in His essence, attributes, and acts, so there is no commonality between Him and other than Him in anything of His essence or of His attributes, such that what is applied to genus and differentia could be applied to Him. Glory be to Him, exalted far above that with great exaltedness, because the genus is a common quality among differing realities.
(p-20) And the differentia is that which separates some of those realities shared in the genus from others. Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, and exalted far above that with great exaltedness.
We will show you that all the attributes, according to their division, have come in the Qur'an as descriptions of both the Creator and the created. In some of that they acknowledge that the Creator is described by them, and that the Qur'an also came describing the created by them; but the description of the Creator is incompatible with the description of the created, just as the essence of the Creator is incompatible with the essence of the created. And what they deny is necessarily analogous to what they affirm, because all of it is of one category, since all the attributes of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are of one category; for the one characterized by them is not resembled by anything of the created things.
From that: the seven attributes, known among them as the attributes of meaning, namely: power (qudrah), will (iradah), knowledge ('ilm), life (hayah), hearing (sam'), sight (basar), and speech (kalam).
Allah, exalted, said in describing Himself with power: ﴿And Allah is over all things Competent﴾ [al-Baqarah: 284], and [Al 'Imran: 29], and [Al 'Imran: 189], and [al-Ma'idah: 19], and [al-Ma'idah: 40], and [al-Anfal: 41].
And He said in describing the originated one with it: ﴿except for those who repent before you gain power over them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 34]. So He affirmed for Himself a true power befitting His majesty and perfection, and affirmed for some originated things a power appropriate to their condition of weakness, dependence, origination, and perishing. Between His power and the power of His creation there is as much incompatibility as between His essence and the essence of His creation.
And He said in describing Himself with will: ﴿Doer of what He intends﴾ [Hud: 107] and [al-Buruj: 16]; ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin: 82]; ﴿Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship﴾ [al-Baqarah: 185], and similar verses.
And He said in describing the created with it: ﴿You desire the commodities of this world﴾ [al-Anfal: 67], the verse; ﴿They do not intend except flight﴾ [al-Ahzab: 13]; ﴿They intend to extinguish the light of Allah﴾ [as-Saff: 8], and similar verses.
So He, Mighty and Majestic, has a true will befitting His perfection and majesty, and the created has a will also appropriate to its condition; and between the will of the Creator and the created there is as much incompatibility as between the essence of the Creator and the created.
And He said in describing Himself with knowledge: ﴿And Allah is Knowing of all things﴾ [an-Nur: 35]; ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has revealed to you; He revealed it with His knowledge﴾, the verse [an-Nisa': 166]; ﴿Then We will surely relate to them with knowledge, and We were not absent﴾ [al-A'raf: 7].
And He said in describing the originated one with it: ﴿They said, "Fear not," and gave him good tidings of a learned boy﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 28]; and He said: ﴿And indeed, he was a possessor of knowledge through what We had taught him﴾ [Yusuf: 68], and similar verses.
So He, Mighty and Majestic, has a true knowledge befitting His perfection and majesty, and the created has a knowledge appropriate to its condition; and between the knowledge of the Creator and the created there is as much incompatibility as between the essence of the Creator and the created.
And He said in describing Himself with life: ﴿Allah – there is no deity except Him, the Living, the Sustainer﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255]; ﴿He is the Living; there is no deity except Him﴾, the verse [Ghafir: 65]; ﴿And rely upon the Living who does not die﴾, the verse [al-Furqan: 58], and similar verses.
And He said in describing the created with it: ﴿And peace be upon him the day he was born, and the day he dies, and the day he is raised alive﴾ [Maryam: 15]; ﴿And We made from water every living thing﴾ [al-Anbiya': 30]; ﴿He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living﴾ [ar-Rum: 19].
So He, Mighty and Majestic, has a true life befitting His majesty and perfection, and the created has also a life appropriate to its condition; and between the life of the Creator and the created there is as much incompatibility as between the essence of the Creator and the created.
And He said in describing Himself with hearing and sight: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾; ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing﴾ [al-Hajj: 75] and [Luqman: 28], and similar verses.
And He said in describing the originated one with them: ﴿Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixture that We may try him; so We made him hearing and seeing﴾ [al-Insan: 2]; ﴿Hear them and see them, the day they come to Us﴾, the verse [Maryam: 38], and similar verses.
So He, Mighty and Majestic, has true hearing and sight befitting His perfection and majesty, and the created has hearing and sight appropriate to its condition; and between the hearing and sight of the Creator, and the hearing and sight of the created, there is as much incompatibility as between the essence of the Creator and the created.
And He said in describing Himself with speech: ﴿And Allah spoke to Moses with direct speech﴾ [an-Nisa': 164]; ﴿I have chosen you above the people by My messages and My speech﴾ [al-A'raf: 144]; ﴿So grant him protection until he hears the speech of Allah﴾ [at-Tawbah: 6], and similar verses.
(p-22) And He said in describing the created with it: ﴿So when he spoke to him, he said, "Indeed, you are today established and trusted in our presence"﴾ [Yusuf: 54]; ﴿That Day We will seal over their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us﴾, the verse [Ya-Sin: 65]; ﴿They said, "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?"﴾ [Maryam: 29], and similar verses.
So He, Mighty and Majestic, has a true speech befitting His perfection and majesty; and the created has speech also appropriate to its condition. And between the speech of the Creator and the created there is as much incompatibility as between the essence of the Creator and the created.
These seven attributes mentioned are affirmed by many who deny other attributes of meaning.
The Mu'tazilah deny them and affirm their rulings, saying: He, exalted, is living, capable, willing, knowing, hearing, seeing, speaking by His essence, not by a power subsisting in His essence, nor by a will subsisting in His essence. Thus, fleeing from them the multiplicity of the Eternal!!
Their false doctrine, whose falsehood and self-contradiction are not hidden from the least intelligent person, because it is known that when the attribute from which derivation is made ceases to exist, derivation from it becomes impossible. So if blackness is absent from a body, for example, it is impossible to say it is black, since it cannot be black without blackness subsisting in it. Likewise, if knowledge and power do not subsist in an entity, it is impossible to say: "It is knowing and powerful," because it is impossible for it to be characterized by them, and knowledge or power does not subsist in it. The author of "Maraqi as-Su'ud" said, in verse [rajaz meter]:
"When the attribute is absent, no derivation is made, and the truth has left the Mu'tazili helpless."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 54 (part 2 of 4):

As for the "moral attributes" (al-sifat al-ma'nawiyyah) according to them, these are the descriptions derived from the seven attributes of meaning mentioned above, namely that He, exalted is He, is: Qadir (Able), Murid (Willing), 'Alim (Knowing), Hayy (Living), Sami' (Hearing), Basir (Seeing), and Mutakallim (Speaking).

The verified position is that these are an expression of the manner of being characterized by the attributes of meaning. The theologians' counting of them as attributes additional to the attributes of meaning is based on what they call the "moral states" (al-ahwal al-ma'nawiyyah), claiming that they are a affirmed matter that is neither existent nor non-existent. The verified truth, about which there is no doubt, is that what they call the "moral states" has no basis at all, and is merely pure imaginings that they imagine. This is because sound reason judges, with a judgment that admits no doubt, that there is absolutely no intermediary between two contradictories. All rational people agree that two contradictories cannot coexist, nor can they both be absent, and there is absolutely no intermediary between them. Thus everything that is not existent is definitely non-existent, and everything that is not non-existent is definitely existent. This is beyond doubt, as you see.

We have already explained, regarding the characterization of the Creator and the created by the attributes of meaning mentioned, the incompatibility of the Creator's attribute with the created. From this you will know its like regarding the characterization by the aforementioned moral attributes, even if we assume they are attributes additional to the attributes of meaning, although the verified position is that they are an expression of the manner of being characterized by them.

As for the "negative attributes" according to them, they are five, and they are, in their view: Qidam (Eternity without beginning), Baqa' (Everlastingness), Wahdaniyyah (Oneness), Mukhalafah lil-khalq (Dissimilarity to creation), and al-Ghina al-mutlaq (Absolute Self-Sufficiency), known among them as al-qiyam bi-l-nafs (self-subsistence).

The criterion of the negative attribute according to them is: it is that which does not indicate, by direct indication (dalalat al-mutabaqah), any existential meaning at all, but only indicates the negation of what is not befitting to God, from God.

As for the attribute that indicates an existential meaning, it is the one known among them as "attribute of meaning." Qidam, for example, has for them no meaning by direct indication except the negation of prior non-existence. If it is said: Power (qudrah), for example, indicates the negation of incapacity ('ajz), knowledge ('ilm) indicates the negation of ignorance (jahl), and life (hayah) indicates the negation of death (mawt), so why do they not call these meanings negative as well?

The answer: Power, for example, indicates by direct indication an existential meaning subsisting in the Essence, namely the attribute by which the bringing into existence of possibilities and their annihilation according to the will is accomplished. It negates incapacity only through a rational premise, namely that reason judges that the subsistence of an existential meaning in the Essence necessarily entails the negation of its opposite from it, because the coexistence of opposites is rationally impossible. The same holds for the rest of the meanings.

As for Qidam according to them, for example, it does not indicate anything additional to what existence indicates, except the negation of prior non-existence. The same holds for the rest of the negative attributes. Having understood this, know that Qidam and Baqa', with which the theologians describe God, the Exalted, claiming that He described Himself with them in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He is the First and the Last﴾ [al-Hadid: 3] — the Noble Qur'an also contains the description of the created with them. He said, describing the created with eternity: ﴿And the moon — We have determined for it phases until it returns like the old dried palm stalk﴾ [Ya-Sin: 39]; He said: ﴿They said, "By God, you are surely in your old error"﴾ [Yusuf: 95]; He said: ﴿Have you considered what you have been worshipping? You and your forefathers, the earlier ones﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 75-76]. He said, describing the created with permanence: ﴿And We made his descendants the remaining ones﴾ [al-Saffat: 77]; He said: ﴿What is with you will end, but what is with God is enduring﴾ [al-Nahl: 96]. Likewise, He described the created with the priority and posteriority mentioned in the verse. He said: ﴿Did We not destroy the former peoples? Then We follow them with the later ones﴾ [al-Mursalat: 16-17]. He described Himself as one, saying: ﴿And your God is one God﴾ [al-Baqarah: 163]; and He said, describing the created with that: ﴿watered with one water﴾ (p-24) And He said, describing Himself with self-sufficiency: ﴿And God is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy﴾ [Fatir: 15]; ﴿And Moses said: If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on earth entirely, then indeed God is Free of need, Praiseworthy﴾ [Ibrahim: 8]; and He said, describing the created with self-sufficiency: ﴿And whoever is wealthy, let him abstain﴾ [al-Nisa': 6]; ﴿If they are poor, God will enrich them﴾ [al-Nur: 32]. He, may He be exalted and glorified, is characterized by those attributes in truth, in the manner befitting His perfection and majesty, and the created is characterized by them also, in the manner appropriate to its origination, its perishing, its incapacity and its need. Between the attributes of the Creator and the created there is as much incompatibility as there is between the Creator and the created, as we have explained regarding the attributes of meaning.

As for the "essential attribute" according to them, it is one: Existence (wujud). You already know what is involved in applying it to God. Some of them made existence identical with the Essence and so did not count it as an attribute, such as Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari. In any case, it is not hidden that the Creator exists and the created exists, and the existence of the Creator negates the existence of the created, as we have explained.

Some of them claimed that Qidam and Baqa' are essential attributes, asserting that they are the two extremes of existence, which in their claim is an essential attribute.

As for the actional attributes (al-sifat al-fi'liyyah), the description of the Creator and the created with them is abundant in the Qur'an, and it is known that the action of the Creator is incompatible with the action of the created, just as His Essence is incompatible with their essence. Among this is His, the Exalted's, description of Himself as providing sustenance to His creatures. He said: ﴿Indeed, God is the Provider﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 58]; ﴿And whatever you spend, He will replace it, and He is the best of providers﴾ [Saba: 39]; and He said: ﴿And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision﴾ [Hud: 6]. He said, describing the created with that: ﴿And when the relatives and the orphans and the needy are present at the division, provide for them from it﴾ [al-Nisa': 8]; and He said: ﴿And upon the father of the child is their provision﴾ [al-Baqarah: 233]. He described Himself with work, saying: ﴿Do they not see that We have created for them, from what Our hands have done, grazing animals?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 71]; and He said, describing the created with it: ﴿You are only recompensed for what you used to do﴾ [al-Tahrim: 7]. He described Himself with teaching His creation, saying: ﴿The Most Merciful. Taught the Qur'an. Created man. Taught him eloquence﴾ [al-Rahman: 1-4].

And He said, describing the created with it: ﴿It is He who raised among the unlettered a messenger from among them, who recites to them His verses and purifies them and teaches them the Book and wisdom﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 2].

He combined the two examples in His saying: ﴿You teach them from what God has taught you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 4]. He described (p-25) Himself as informing (yunabbi'), and described the created with that, and He combined the two examples in His saying: ﴿And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement. And when she informed [of it], and God caused him to know of it, he made known part of it and ignored part. So when he informed her of it, she said, "Who told you this?" He said, "The All-Knowing, All-Acquainted informed me"﴾ [al-Tahrim: 3].

He described Himself with giving, saying: ﴿Have you not considered the one who argued with Abraham concerning his Lord, because God had given him kingship?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 258]; He said: ﴿He gives wisdom to whom He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah: 269]; He said: ﴿And He gives every doer of virtue his virtue﴾ [Hud: 3]; He said: ﴿That is the bounty of God, which He gives to whom He wills﴾ [al-Hadid: 21].

And He said, describing the created with that: ﴿And you have given one of them a heap of gold﴾ [al-Nisa': 20]; ﴿And give the orphans their properties﴾ [al-Nisa': 2]; ﴿And give the women their dowries graciously﴾ [al-Nisa': 4]. Examples of this are very numerous in the Mighty Qur'an.

It is known that what God is described with of these actions is established for Him in truth, in the manner befitting His perfection and majesty; and what the created is described with of them is established for it also, in the manner appropriate to its condition. Between the description of the Creator and the created there is as much incompatibility as there is between the essence of the Creator and the created.

As for the "comprehensive attributes" (al-sifat al-jami'ah), such as greatness (al-'izam), magnificence (al-kibar), exaltation (al-'uluww), kingship (al-mulk), arrogance (al-takabbur) and tyranny (al-jabarut), and the like, the description of the Creator and the created with them is also very frequent in the Noble Qur'an.

It is known that what the Creator is described with of them is incompatible with what the created is described with, just as the essence of the Creator is incompatible with the essence of the created.
