He said, describing Himself, may He be exalted, with exaltation, greatness and magnificence: ﴿And it does not burden Him to preserve them, and He is the Most High, the Most Great﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255]; ﴿Indeed, God is ever Exalted and Great﴾ [al-Nisa': 34]; ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Grand, the Exalted﴾ [al-Ra'd: 9].

He said, describing the created with greatness: ﴿So each division was like a great mountain﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 63]; ﴿Indeed, you are saying a terrible saying﴾ [al-Isra': 40]; ﴿And she has a great throne﴾ [al-Naml: 23]; ﴿Upon Him I have relied, and He is the Lord of the Great Throne﴾ [al-Tawbah: 129], and other verses.

He said, describing the created with greatness of size: ﴿For them is forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [al-Mulk: 12]; he said: ﴿Indeed, their killing was a great sin﴾ [al-Isra': 31]; he said: ﴿If you do not do it, there will be fitnah on earth and great corruption﴾ [al-Anfal: 73]; he said: ﴿And indeed, it would have been difficult except for those whom God guided﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]; he said: ﴿And indeed, it is difficult except for the humbly submissive﴾ [al-Baqarah: 45].

(p-26) He said, describing the created with exaltedness: ﴿And We raised him to a high station﴾ [Maryam: 57]; ﴿And We granted them a true tongue of high repute﴾ [Maryam: 50], and other verses.

He said, describing Himself with kingship: ﴿Glorifying God is whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, the King, the Pure﴾ [al-Hashr: 23]; ﴿He is God, other than whom there is no deity, the King, the Pure﴾ [al-Hashr: 23]; and He said: ﴿In a seat of truth, in the presence of a Perfectly Capable King﴾ [al-Qamar: 55].

He said, describing the created with it: ﴿And the king said, "Indeed, I see seven fat cows"﴾ [Yusuf: 43]; ﴿And the king said, "Bring him to me"﴾ [Yusuf: 50]; ﴿And there was behind them a king who seized every boat by force﴾ [al-Kahf: 79]; ﴿How will he have kingship over us when we are more deserving of kingship than he?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 247]; ﴿You give kingship to whom You will and You take kingship away from whom You will﴾ [Al 'Imran: 26], and other verses.

He said, describing Himself with might: ﴿And if you slip after clear proofs have come to you, then know that God is Almighty, All-Wise﴾ [al-Baqarah: 209]; ﴿Glorifying God is whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, the King, the Pure, the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 1]; ﴿Or do they possess the treasuries of the mercy of your Lord, the Almighty, the Bestower?﴾ [Sad: 9].

He said, describing the created with might: ﴿The wife of the 'Aziz said...﴾ [Yusuf: 51]; ﴿And he said, "Entrust her to me," and he overpowered me in speech﴾ [Sad: 23].

He said, describing Himself, may He be exalted, as Jabbar and Mutakabbir: ﴿He is God, other than whom there is no deity, the King, the Pure, the Peace, the Giver of Security, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Compeller, the Majestic﴾ [al-Hashr: 23].

He said, describing the created with both: ﴿Thus God seals every heart of an arrogant tyrant﴾ [Ghafir: 35]; ﴿Is there not in Hell a residence for the arrogant?﴾ [al-Zumar: 60]; ﴿And when you strike, you strike as tyrants﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 130], and other verses.

He said, describing Himself with strength: ﴿Indeed, God is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 58]; ﴿And God will surely support whoever supports Him. Indeed, God is Powerful and Mighty﴾ [al-Hajj: 40].

He said, describing the created with it: ﴿"Who is stronger than us in strength?" Did they not see that God, who created them, is stronger than them in strength?﴾ [Fussilat: 15]; ﴿And He will increase you in strength upon your strength﴾ [Hud: 52]; ﴿Indeed, the best one you could hire is the strong and trustworthy﴾ [al-Qasas: 26]; ﴿God is the One who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength﴾ [al-Rum: 54] (p-27) and other verses.

Examples of these comprehensive attributes are numerous in the Qur'an. It is known that He, may He be exalted, is characterized by these mentioned attributes in truth, in the manner befitting His perfection and majesty. What the created is described with of them is incompatible with what the Creator is described with, just as the essence of the Creator, may He be exalted, is incompatible with the essences of created things. There is no difficulty in any of this. Likewise are the attributes about which the theologians have differed: whether they are among the attributes of meaning or among the attributes of actions. Although the truth, which is not hidden from one whom God has illuminated in insight, is that they are attributes of meaning which God, may He be exalted, affirmed for Himself, like compassion (al-ra'fah) and mercy (al-rahmah).

He said, describing Him, may He be exalted, with both:

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 54 (part 3 of 4):

﴿Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful﴾ [an-Nahl: 47]. And He described our Prophet (ﷺ) with both of these attributes: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. He is grieved by your suffering, concerned over you, and to the believers he is kind and merciful﴾ [at-Tawbah: 128]. And He described Himself with forbearance: ﴿He will surely admit them to an entrance they will be pleased with, and indeed Allah is Knowing and Forbearing﴾ [al-Hajj: 59].

He also described the one who is created with it: ﴿So We gave him the good news of a forbearing boy﴾ [as-Saffat: 101], and ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was compassionate and forbearing﴾ [at-Tawbah: 114].

He described Himself with forgiveness: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Baqarah: 182], [al-Ma'idah: 34], [al-Ma'idah: 39], [al-Ma'idah: 98], [al-Anfal: 69], [at-Tawbah: 5], [at-Tawbah: 99], [at-Tawbah: 102], [an-Nur: 62], [al-'Ankabut: 14], [al-Mumtahanah: 12], [al-Muzzammil: 20]. ﴿For them is forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [al-Hujurat: 3], and similar verses.

He described the one who is created with it: ﴿And whoever is patient and forgives, indeed that is of the matters requiring determination﴾ [ash-Shura: 43]. ﴿Say to those who believe: forgive those who do not expect the days of Allah﴾ (the verse) [al-Jathiyah: 14]. ﴿A kind word and forgiveness are better than charity followed by harm﴾ [al-Baqarah: 263], and similar verses.

He, Exalted is He, described Himself with good pleasure, and He also described the created one with it, saying: ﴿Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 119]. He described Himself, Exalted is He, with love, and described the created one with it, saying: ﴿Allah will bring a people whom He loves and who love Him, humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers, striving in the way of Allah and not fearing the blame of any blamer﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 54]. ﴿Say: If you should love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 31].

He described Himself as becoming angry when His sanctities are violated, saying: ﴿Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that as a recompense from Allah? Those whom Allah has cursed and with whom He is angry﴾ (the verse) [al-Ma'idah: 60]. ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein, and Allah will be angry with him﴾ (the verse) [an-Nisa': 93].

He described the created one with anger: ﴿And when Musa returned to his people, angry and grieved﴾ [al-A'raf: 150]. Examples of this are very numerous.

Our purpose here is to mention many examples of this, while clarifying that every attribute with which Exalted is He is described reaches the extremes of perfection, loftiness and nobility, which cuts off the ties of every illusion of resemblance between the attributes of Exalted is He and the attributes of His creation, glorified is He and exalted above that by a great exaltation.

* *

When you have verified all of this, you will know that He, Exalted is He, described Himself with istiwa' (rising/settling) over the Throne, and described others with istiwa' over some of the created things. He, Exalted is He, praised Himself in seven verses of His Book for His istiwa' over His Throne, and He mentioned the attribute of istiwa' only in conjunction with other attributes of perfection and majesty, which point to His greatness and majesty, Exalted is He, and that He alone is the Lord, the one deserving to be worshipped alone.

The first place, according to the arrangement of the noble Mushaf: His saying here in surah al-A'raf: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days; then He rose over the Throne. He covers the night with the day, which it follows rapidly, and [He created] the sun, the moon, and the stars, subjected by His command. Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [7: 54].

The second place: His saying, Exalted is He, in surah Yunus: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days; then He rose over the Throne, arranging the affair. There is no intercessor except after His permission. That is Allah, your Lord, so worship Him. Will you not be reminded?﴾ ﴿To Him is your return, all of you, as a promise of Allah, true. Indeed, He originates creation and then repeats it﴾ (the verse) [10: 3, 4].

The third place: His saying, Exalted is He, in surah ar-Ra'd: ﴿Allah is the One who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see; then He rose over the Throne and subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term. He arranges the affair and details the signs that you may be certain of the meeting with your Lord﴾ ﴿And it is He who spread out the earth and placed therein firm mountains and rivers, and of all fruits He placed therein two mates, two. He covers the night with the day. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect﴾ ﴿And on the earth are neighboring tracts, gardens of grapevines, crops, and palm trees, some multiple-stemmed and some single-stemmed, watered with one water, yet We favor some of them over others in fruit. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason﴾ [13: 2, 3, 4].

The fourth place: His saying, Exalted is He, in surah Ta-Ha: ﴿We did not send down to you the Qur'an for you to be distressed﴾ ﴿but as a reminder to whoever fears﴾ ﴿a revelation from He who created the earth and the high heavens﴾ ﴿The Most Merciful rose over the Throne﴾ ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is beneath the soil﴾ [20: 2–6].

The fifth place: His saying in surah al-Furqan: ﴿And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die, and exalt Him with His praise, and sufficient is He as Knower of the sins of His servants﴾ ﴿He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days; then He rose over the Throne. The Most Merciful, so ask about Him one who is informed﴾ [25: 58, 59].

The sixth place: His saying, Exalted is He, in surah as-Sajdah: ﴿Allah is the One who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days; then He rose over the Throne. You have not besides Him any protector or intercessor. Will you not remember?﴾ ﴿He arranges the affair from the heaven to the earth﴾ (the verse) [32: 4, 5].

The seventh place: His saying, Exalted is He, in surah al-Hadid: ﴿He is the One who created the heavens and the earth in six days; then He rose over the Throne. He knows what enters into the earth and what emerges from it, and what descends from the heaven and what ascends therein. And He is with you wherever you are﴾ [57: 4].

Exalted is He also said, describing the created thing with istiwa' over some of the created things: ﴿That you may sit firmly upon its back and then remember the favor of your Lord when you are seated upon it﴾ (the verse) [az-Zukhruf: 13]. ﴿And when you and those with you have settled upon the ship﴾ (the verse) [al-Mu'minun: 28]. ﴿And it settled upon al-Judi﴾ (the verse) [Hud: 44], and similar verses.

From what has preceded, you know that there is no difficulty in this matter: the Creator, Exalted is He, has an istiwa' befitting His perfection and majesty, and the created being also has an istiwa' suited to its condition. Between the istiwa' of the Creator and the created being there is as much incompatibility as there is between the essence of the Creator and the created being, as in ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾, as its clarification has previously been explained.

The one who considers this question should reflect upon several matters:

The first matter: all attributes belong to one category, because the one described by them is one, and it is not permissible concerning Him to liken Him to created things in any of their attributes. Whoever affirms, for example, that He is All-Hearing and All-Seeing, while holding that His hearing and sight are unlike the hearing and sight of created beings, is necessarily bound to the same for all attributes, such as istiwa', yad (hand), and similar attributes of His, Exalted is He, and there is no possible way to distinguish between these.

The second matter: the essence and the attributes also belong to one category. Just as He, Exalted is He, has an essence unlike all the essences of creation, so He, Exalted is He, has attributes unlike all the attributes of creation.

The third matter: in establishing the position regarding the apparent meaning that comes immediately to the understanding from verses of the attributes, such as istiwa' and yad for example.

Know first that a countless multitude of the later scholars have erred in this, claiming that the apparent meaning that comes immediately to the understanding from the meaning of istiwa' and yad, for instance, in the Qur'anic verses, is the likeness of the attributes of created beings. They said: it is obligatory for us to turn it away from its apparent meaning by consensus (ijma'), because believing in its apparent meaning is disbelief, since whoever likens the Creator to the created is a disbeliever. Yet it is not hidden from even the least intelligent person that the true meaning of this statement is that Allah described Himself in His Book with what its apparent and immediately understood meaning is disbelief in Allah and speaking about Him in a way that is unfitting for Him, Exalted is He.

And the Prophet (ﷺ), to whom it was said: ﴿And We sent down to you the Reminder, that you may explain to the people what has been sent down to them﴾ [an-Nahl: 44], did not explain a single letter of that, along with the consensus of those among the scholars whose opinion counts, that he (ﷺ) is not permitted to delay explanation beyond the time of need for it, and all the more so in matters of creed, especially what its apparent and immediately understood meaning is disbelief and manifest misguidance. Then these ignorant people of the later generations came and claimed that Allah applied to Himself descriptions whose apparent meaning is unfitting, and that the Prophet (ﷺ) concealed that this apparent meaning is disbelief and misguidance, which requires turning the wording away from it. All of this is from their own opinions, without reliance on a Book or Sunnah. Glory be to You, this is a tremendous slander.

It is not hidden that this statement is among the greatest misguidance and among the most serious fabrication against Allah, Exalted is He, and His Messenger (ﷺ). The truth about which no intelligent person has any doubt is that every attribute with which Allah described Himself, or with which His Messenger (ﷺ) described Him, its apparent and immediately understood meaning for whoever has some faith in his heart is complete transcendence above resemblance to any attribute of created things.

The understanding that comes immediately to every intelligent person is that the Creator is distinct from the created in His essence and in all His attributes. No one denies this except an arrogant obstinate person.

The ignorant fabricator who claims that the apparent meaning of the verses of attributes is unfitting for Allah, because it is disbelief and likeness, has been led to this only by the defilement of his heart with resemblance, to the degree of that resemblance between the Creator and the created. The ill omen of likening led him to deny the attributes of Allah, Exalted is He, and not to believe in them, although He, Exalted is He, is the One who described Himself with them. So this ignorant person became a likener at first and a denier afterward, and committed what is unfitting for Allah from beginning to end. Had his heart known Allah as it should, and glorified Allah as it should, and been pure from the filth of likening, then the understanding that would come immediately to him would be that the description of Allah, Exalted is He, reaches such a level of perfection and majesty that it cuts off the illusions of ties of resemblance between Him and the attributes of created beings. His heart would then be prepared to believe in the attributes of perfection and majesty established for Allah in the Qur'an and the authentic Sunnah, together with complete transcendence above resemblance to the attributes of creation, as in His saying: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾. If an over-zealous person were to say: "Explain to us the manner of being described by the attributes of istiwa' and yad, and similar, so that we may understand them," we would say: "Do you know the manner of the holy essence that is described by those attributes?"

He must say: "No." We would then say: knowing the manner of being described by the attributes depends on knowing the manner of the essence. Glory be to Him, whom no one else can enumerate His praise, as He praised Himself: ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them, but they cannot encompass Him in knowledge﴾ [Ta-Ha: 110]. ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾. ﴿Say: He is Allah, One﴾ ﴿Allah, the Eternal Refuge﴾ ﴿He neither begets nor is born﴾ ﴿Nor is there to Him any equivalent﴾ [al-Ikhlas: 1–4]. ﴿So do not set forth examples for Allah﴾ [an-Nahl: 74].

From all of this research it becomes established that the attributes belong to one category, and that the truth regarding them is composed of two matters:

The first: the transcendence of Allah, Exalted is He, above resemblance to the creation.

The second: belief in everything with which He described Himself, or with which His Messenger (ﷺ) described Him, whether affirmation or negation. This is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾. The pious predecessors (Salaf), may Allah be pleased with them, did not doubt anything of that, nor was it difficult for them. Do you not see the saying of al-Farazdaq, who was a poet only, and in terms of knowledge was a commoner [at-Tawil]:

"And how should I fear people, when Allah holds the people and the [seven heavens and earths] in the palm of His hand?"

And what he means by the seventy is seven heavens and seven earths. Whoever knows, from the fact that the heavens and the earths are in the hand of Him, exalted and high is He, [even] less than a mustard seed, is a knower of the greatness and majesty of Allah. Nothing comes to his mind of the resemblance of His attributes to the attributes of creation. Whoever is like this, many of the difficulties that perplexed many of the later scholars fall away from him. And this which we have mentioned, of the transcendence of Allah, exalted and high is He, above what is not befitting to Him, and of belief in what He described Himself with, or what His Messenger ﷺ described Him with, is the meaning of the saying of Imam Malik, may Allah have mercy on him: "The istiwa' (settling) is not unknown, the how (kayf) is not conceivable, and asking about it is an innovation (bid'ah)."

A saying similar to this saying of Malik is narrated from his teacher Rabi'ah ibn Abi 'Abd al-Rahman, and from Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 56:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good.﴾

In this noble verse He mentions that His mercy, may He be exalted and high, is near to His servants who do good. In another place He clarified the attributes of His servants for whom He will prescribe it, in His saying: ﴿And My mercy encompasses all things, so I will prescribe it for those who fear Me and give zakah﴾ [al-A'raf: 156], to the end of the verse.

As for the reason the predicate is masculine (qarib, "near") although mercy (rahmah) is feminine, and He did not say qariba, the scholars have more than ten opinions on it. We will mention some of them, if Allah wills, and leave aside those whose weakness or remoteness from the apparent meaning is evident to us.

Among them: mercy (rahmah) is a verbal noun (masdar) in the sense of the womb (rahim), so the masculine is used in consideration of the meaning.

Among them: it is one of the features of the Arabic language that when kinship is a kinship of lineage, the feminine is required for a female, so you say: "This woman is my qaribah (female relative)," meaning in lineage, and you do not say qarib minni. If it is a kinship of distance, both the masculine and feminine are permitted, so you say: "His house is qarib and qaribah from me." This view is supported by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour is near﴾ [al-Shura: 17], and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And what will make you know? Perhaps the Hour will be near﴾ [al-Ahzab: 63], and the saying of Imru' al-Qays: [Tawil]

To him is woe, if Umm Hashim is not near, nor al-Basbasah, daughter of Yashkur.

Among them: the reason is the attribution of mercy to Allah, may He be exalted.

Among them: His saying qarib is an adjective of a deleted noun, meaning "a thing near to the doers of good."

Among them: it has been likened to fa'il in the sense of maf'ul, which is used equally for male and female.

Among them: nouns in the pattern fa'il are sometimes likened to the verbal noun in the pattern fa'il, and so they are used in the singular. Some of them said: For this reason He used the singular ṣadiq (friend) in His saying: ﴿or [from] what you possess its keys, or a friend of yours﴾ [al-Nur: 61], and in the saying of the poet: [Mutaqarib]

And they are a friend to whoever has not grown old

End of quote. And ẓahir (helper) in His saying: ﴿and the angels, after that, are a helper﴾ [al-Tahrim: 4], and other aspects besides these.

**The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿It is He who sends the winds as heralds of good news before His mercy﴾ [al-A'raf: 57].**

The reading of ʿĀṣim (the recitation, *qirāʾa*, of ʿĀṣim) is *bushran* with a *ḍamma* on the *bāʾ* and the *shīn* sukun, which is the plural of *bashīr* (bearer of good news), because the winds spread out ahead of the rain, bringing good tidings of it. This meaning is clarified by the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And among His signs is that He sends the winds as heralds of good news﴾, the verse [al-Rum: 46], and by His words: ﴿before His mercy﴾ [al-A'raf: 57], meaning by His mercy the rain, as it is explained in other places, such as His words: ﴿And it is He who sends down the rain after they have despaired, and spreads His mercy﴾, the verse [al-Shura: 28], and His words: ﴿So look at the traces of the mercy of Allah, how He gives life to the earth after its death﴾.

* *

**The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Until, when they have carried heavy clouds, We drive them to a dead land﴾**, the verse [al-Shura: 28].

In this noble verse He explains that He carries the clouds upon the wind, then drives them to whichever parts of the earth He wills. He clarifies this meaning in many verses, such as His words: ﴿And Allah is the One who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds, and We drive them to a dead land﴾, the verse [Fatir: 9], and His words: ﴿Do they not see that We drive the water to the barren land and bring forth thereby crops from which eat their livestock and themselves? Will they not see?﴾ [al-Sajda: 27], and other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 63:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do you wonder that a reminder from your Lord has come to you through a man from among you, so that he may warn you?﴾ and so on. In this noble surah, Allah, exalted is He, rebuked the people of Nuh and the people of Hud for their wonder at the sending of a man. He also made clear in other places that all nations wondered at this. Regarding the wonder of the people of our Prophet ﷺ at this, He said: ﴿Is it a wonder for the people that We revealed to a man from among them, [saying], "Warn the people"?﴾ [Yunus: 2]. He said: ﴿Rather, they wondered that a warner from among themselves came to them﴾ and so on [Qaf: 2]. And He said concerning the earlier nations: ﴿That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, and they said, "Would humans guide us?" So they disbelieved and turned away, and Allah was self-sufficient. And Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴾ [At-Taghabun: 6]. He said: ﴿Thamud denied the warnings and said, "Shall we follow a single human from among us?"﴾ and so on [Al-Qamar: 23-24]. He said: ﴿And if you obey a human like yourselves, then you would surely be losers﴾ [Al-Muminun: 34]. He also declared that this wonder at the sending of a human being prevents people from faith, in His saying: ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ [Al-Isra: 94].

Allah answered them on this in many verses:

• such as His saying: ﴿And We did not send before you except men﴾ and so on [Al-Anbiya: 7],

• and His saying: ﴿And We did not send before you any messengers except that they ate food and walked in the markets﴾ and so on [Al-Furqan: 20],

• and His saying: ﴿And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man﴾ and so on [Al-An'am: 9],

and other verses besides these.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And We drowned those who denied Our signs.﴾

He did not explain here the manner of their drowning, but He explained it in other places, such as His saying: ﴿So We opened the gates of heaven with water pouring forth﴾ [al-Qamar: 11], and His saying: ﴿So the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 14].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 71:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do you dispute with me over names which you and your fathers have named?﴾ and the rest of the verse. Here He did not explain anything of this dispute that took place between Hud, upon him and upon our Prophet be prayers and peace, and 'Ad. But He alluded to it in other places, such as His saying: ﴿They said, "O Hud, you have not brought us any clear proof, and we will not leave our gods on your word, nor will we believe in you."﴾ ﴿We say nothing except that some of our gods have struck you with evil." He said, "Indeed, I call Allah to witness, and you bear witness, that I am free from what you associate ﴾ ﴿other than Him. So plot against me all together, then do not give me respite.﴾ ﴿Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path.﴾

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 72:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We cut off the root of those who denied Our signs﴾ — the verse.

He does not explain here the manner of His cutting off the root of 'Ad, but He explained it in other places, such as His saying: ﴿As for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a furious, violent wind﴾ — the verse [al-Haqqah: 6], and His saying: ﴿And in 'Ad, when We sent upon them the barren wind﴾ — the verse [adh-Dhariyat: 41], and similar verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 77:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So they hamstrung the she-camel﴾ and the rest of the verse.

The apparent meaning of this noble verse is that a group of people carried out the hamstringing of her. However, He, exalted is He, clarified in Surah al-Qamar that what is meant is that they called out to one of their number, and he undertook the hamstringing of her. This is in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But they called their companion, and he took (it) in hand and hamstrung (it)﴾ [29].

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they said, "O Salih, bring us what you have been promising us"﴾ and the rest of the verse.

He did not specify here what it was that he promised them, but He clarified in other places that it was the punishment:

• As in His saying: ﴿And do not touch her with harm, lest there seize you the punishment of a near (day)﴾ [Hud: 64],

• And His saying here: ﴿So there will seize you a painful punishment﴾ [al-A'raf: 73],

• And His saying: ﴿Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days; that is a promise not to be denied﴾ [Hud: 65],

and similar to that of the verses.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 78:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So the earthquake seized them, and they became in their home prostrate corpses﴾. He did not explain here the cause of the earth's quaking beneath them; but He explained in another place that the cause of that was the shout (ṣayḥah) of the angel upon them, namely His saying: ﴿And those who did wrong were seized by the shout﴾ [Hud: 67] - the verse. The apparent meaning is that when the angel shouted at them, the earth quaked beneath them because of the intensity of the shout, and their souls departed from their bodies. And Allah, may He be exalted and glorified, knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 79:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So he turned away from them and said, "O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord"﴾.

And Allah, exalted is He, explained this message which His prophet Salih conveyed to his people in many verses, such as His saying: ﴿And to Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. There has already come to you clear evidence from your Lord. This is the she-camel of Allah as a sign to you, so leave her to eat within Allah's earth and do not touch her with harm, lest there seize you a painful punishment."﴾.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Do you commit an abomination that no one in all the worlds has committed before you?﴾

Allah, the Exalted, made clear that the intended meaning of this abomination is sodomy (liwat, the act of male-with-male intercourse), by His words after it: ﴿Indeed, you approach men with desire instead of women﴾ [al-A'raf: 81]. He also made this clear by His words: ﴿Do you approach the males among the worlds?﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 165], and His words: ﴿And you commit within your gatherings the evil [practice]﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 29].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 83:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We saved him and his family﴾.

The apparent meaning of this noble verse is that only the specific members of his family were saved along with Lut. Allah, exalted is He, made this clear in Surat adh-Dhariyat with His saying: ﴿So We brought out whoever was in it of the believers. But We found not in it except one house of Muslims﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 35-36]. And His saying here: ﴿except his wife; she was of those who remained behind﴾ [al-A'raf: 83] is clarified in other places. He made clear that she was a traitor, that she was among the people of the Fire, and that she was subject to what befell her people of destruction. He said concerning her and the wife of Nuh: ﴿Allah presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Nuh and the wife of Lut. They were under two of Our righteous servants, but they betrayed them, so they availed them nothing against Allah, and it was said, "Enter the Fire with those who enter."﴾ [at-Tahrim: 10]. And He said concerning her alone, meaning the wife of Lut: ﴿except your wife; indeed, she will be struck by what strikes them﴾, the verse [Hud: 81]. (p-36) His saying here concerning the people of Lut: ﴿And We rained upon them a rain, so look how was the end of the criminals﴾ [al-A'raf: 84].

Here it does not specify what this rain was, but He made clear in other places that it was a rain of stones with which Allah destroyed them, as in His saying: ﴿And We rained upon them stones of sijjil﴾ [al-Hijr: 74]. He indicated that sijjil is clay by His saying in adh-Dhariyat: ﴿to send upon them stones of clay﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 33]. He also made clear that this rain was a rain of evil, not of mercy, by His saying: ﴿And they have certainly passed by the town which was rained upon with a rain of evil﴾ [al-Furqan: 40], and His saying, exalted is He, in ash-Shu'ara': ﴿And We rained upon them a rain, and wretched was the rain of those who were warned﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 173].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 86:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you bar from the path of Allah whoever believes in Him, and seek to make it crooked﴾.

The pronoun in His saying "and seek to make it [tabghunaha] crooked" refers back to "the path" (al-sabil), and this is a Qur'anic textual indication that al-sabil is feminine. However, there occurs in another passage something that also indicates that al-sabil is masculine, and that is His saying, exalted is He, in this noble surah: ﴿And if they see the way of guidance, they will not adopt it as a way; but if they see the way of error, they will adopt it as a way﴾ [al-A'raf: 146].

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 7, verse 87:**

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And if there is a group among you who has believed in that with which I have been sent, and a group who has not believed, then be patient until Allah judges between us. And He is the best of judges.﴾

Allah, may He be exalted, explained the judgment He passed upon them with His statement: ﴿And when Our command came, We saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him by mercy from Us, and the blast seized those who had wronged﴾ [Hud: 94],

• and His statement: ﴿So the quake seized them, and they became within their home prostrate corpses﴾ [al-A'raf: 78],

• and His statement: ﴿Those who denied Shu'ayb became as if they had never prospered therein. Those who denied Shu'ayb were the losers﴾ [al-A'raf: 92],

• and His statement: ﴿So the punishment of the Day of the Shade seized them﴾ and the verse [al-Shu'ara': 189].

If it is said: Allah mentioned that the destruction which befell the people of Shu'ayb was a quake in al-A'raf, mentioned in Hud that it was a blast (sayhah), and mentioned in al-Shu'ara' that it was the punishment of the Day of the Shade.

The answer is what Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his tafsir (exegesis). He said: "All of that gathered upon them. The punishment of the Day of the Shade befell them, which was a cloud that overshadowed them, in which there were sparks of fire, flames, and a great blaze. Then a blast came upon them from the sky, and a violent quake from the earth beneath them. So the souls departed, the spirits flowed out, and the bodies became still." End of quotation from him.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 93:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So he turned away from them and said, "O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you, so how could I grieve over a disbelieving people?"﴾

Exalted and high is He, has made clear the messages which His Messenger Shu'ayb conveyed to his people (p-37) in many verses,

• such as His saying: ﴿And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. And do not diminish the measure and the scale..."﴾ [Hud: 84], and similar verses from the Qur'an. He also made clear his counsel to them in many verses,

• such as His saying: ﴿And O my people, let not my dissension cause you to incur [a punishment] like that which struck the people of Noah or the people of Hud or the people of Salih. And the people of Lot are not far from you.﴾ [Hud: 89],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So how could I grieve over a disbelieving people?﴾ [al-A'raf: 93]. The Prophet of Allah Shu'ayb, upon him and upon our Prophet be prayers and peace, disapproved of grief (al-asa), that is, sorrow over the disbelievers when Allah destroys them after he has conveyed the message to them and established the proof against them, while they persist in disbelief and transgression out of obstinacy and stubbornness. His disapproval of this indicates that it is not befitting, and Allah, exalted is He, has stated this explicitly, and so He forbade our Prophet ﷺ from it in His saying: ﴿And many of them will surely increase in transgression and disbelief from what has been revealed to you from your Lord. So do not grieve over the disbelieving people.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 68]. The meaning of "do not grieve" (la ta'sa) is: do not be sorrowful,

• and His saying: ﴿And do not grieve over them﴾ [al-Nahl: 127].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 101:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Such were the cities; We relate to you some of their tidings﴾.

He mentioned their tidings in detail in many places, such as the verses in which the account of Nuh (Noah), Hud, Salih, Lut (Lot), Shu'ayb and others is given, together with their peoples, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them.

* *

The words of the Most High: ﴿So they would not have believed in what they had denied before﴾. Concerning this noble verse, the scholars have several interpretations (awjuh min al-tafsir), some of which are supported by the Qur'an.

Among them: the meaning is that they would not have believed in what Allah had already known, at the time He took the covenant (al-mithaq), that they would deny it and not believe in it. This is because the change of what the eternal knowledge (al-'ilm al-azali) has already determined is impossible. This view is narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Anas, and al-Tabari (Ibn Jarir) chose it. Many verses support this interpretation, such as His saying: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified will not believe﴾ [Yunus: 96], and His saying: ﴿And signs and warnings do not avail a people who do not believe﴾ [Yunus: 101], and similar verses.

Among them: the meaning of the verse is that the covenant was taken from them, and they believed under compulsion (karhan), so they would not have believed willingly after that. This is narrated from al-Suddi, and it returns in meaning to the first view.

Among them: the meaning of the verse is that if they were returned to the world once more, they would still disbelieve. So they would not have believed, upon being returned to the world, in what they had denied before, that is, the first time. This is narrated from Mujahid. The words of the Most High support the meaning of this view: ﴿And if they were returned, they would certainly return to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-An'am: 28]. However, this is far from the apparent meaning of the verse.

(p-38) Among them: the meaning of the verse is that they would not have believed in what the Messengers brought, because of their denial of the truth at the very first time it reached them. This view was related by Ibn 'Atiyyah, and Ibn Kathir approved it, and it is one of the views closest to the apparent meaning of this noble verse. Its basis is clear, for the evil consequence of hastening to deny the Messengers is a cause of the sealing of hearts and distance from guidance. The verses indicating this meaning are many, such as:

• His saying: ﴿Rather, Allah has sealed their hearts because of their disbelief﴾ [al-Nisa: 155],

• His saying: ﴿So when they deviated, Allah caused their hearts to deviate﴾ [al-Saff: 5],

• His saying: ﴿In their hearts is a disease, so Allah increased them in disease﴾ [al-Baqarah: 10],

• His saying: ﴿That is because they believed, then disbelieved, so their hearts were sealed﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 3],

and other verses besides these.

We have already mentioned, in the introduction to this blessed book, that a verse may have several interpretations, all of which are supported by the Qur'an, and all of which are true. So we mention all of them, and knowledge is with Allah, the Most High.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 103:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then after them We sent Musa with Our signs to Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they wronged them thereby⦆ ... the verse.

Here He, exalted is He, makes clear that Pharaoh and his chiefs (mala'uhu) wronged by means of the signs that Musa brought them. In Surah an-Naml He states explicitly that they did this while denying them, even though they were certain within themselves that they were true, out of their wrongdoing and arrogance. This is in His saying: ﴿And when Our signs came to them, plainly visible, they said, "This is manifest magic." And they denied them, though their souls were convinced of them, out of wrongdoing and haughtiness﴾ [an-Naml 27:13].

The author said, under the heading "Removing the appearance of contradiction from the verses of the Book":

His words, exalted is He: ﴿So he threw down his staff, and behold, it became a manifest serpent﴾, and the rest of the verse.

This verse indicates that the staff was likened to a thu'ban (a large serpent), and this word is applied only to a large snake. Another verse has come indicating something different, namely His words, exalted is He: ﴿When he saw it moving as though it were a jann﴾, and the rest of the verse [An-Naml: 10], because the jann is a small snake.

The answer to this is that He likened it to the thu'ban in the greatness of its form, and to the jann in its trembling, its lightness, and the speed of its movement. So it combined greatness with lightness of movement, contrary to what is customary.

The Quranic words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And he drew his hand out, and behold, it was white to the onlookers﴾.

Allah, the Exalted, mentions here that Musa drew out his hand and behold, it was white. He does not state here that this whiteness was free of leprosy (baras). He does, however, make this clear in the surahs of "al-Naml" and "al-Qasas," in His words in both: ﴿it will come out white, without any defect﴾ [Yusuf: 32], meaning without leprosy (baras).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 109:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The chiefs of the people of Pharaoh said, "Indeed, this is a learned magician."﴾

Here he explains that when Musa brought the sign of the staff and the hand, the chiefs of the people of Pharaoh said that he is a magician. He did not mention what Pharaoh himself said. However, he made clear in "al-Shu'ara'" (The Poets) that Pharaoh said the same as what the chiefs of his people said, and that is in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said to the chiefs around him, "Indeed, this is a learned magician."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 34].

He did not specify here what this great magic was, nor did he say whether Musa (Moses) sensed fear of it within himself. But he explained all of that in "Ta-Ha," in his words: ﴿Then their ropes and their staffs appeared to him, by their magic, to be moving. So Musa felt a fear within himself. We said, "Do not fear; indeed, you are the superior. And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow what they have made. What they have made is only the plot of a magician, and a magician does not succeed wherever he goes."﴾ [al-Tahrim: - 96] (p-39). He also did not mention here that they had arranged with Musa an appointed time for the contest with the magicians. He clarified that in the surah "Ta-Ha," in their statement: ﴿So we will surely bring you magic like it. Set between us and you an appointment which neither we nor you will fail to keep, at a neutral place.﴾ ﴿He said, "Your appointment is the Day of Adornment."﴾ [al-Mujadilah: - 59], to the end of the verse.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 124:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then I will surely crucify you all﴾.

He did not specify here the matter in which he threatened them that he would crucify them, but he specified it in another place, as in His saying in "Ta-Ha": ﴿And I will surely crucify you upon the trunks of palm trees﴾ [20:71], the verse.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But when a misfortune befalls them, they attribute it to Moses and those with him﴾.

Exalted is He mentions in this noble verse that when Pharaoh and his people were struck by a misfortune, meaning drought, dearth and the like, they attributed it to Moses and his people, saying: ﴿This drought and dearth has come upon us only because of your ill omen﴾. Something similar was mentioned of some of the disbelievers with our Prophet (ﷺ) in His saying: ﴿But when a misfortune befalls them, they say, "This is from you"﴾ [An-Nisa: 78]. Something similar was also mentioned of the people of Salih with Salih in His saying: ﴿They said, "We consider you and those with you to be a bad omen"﴾ [An-Naml: 47]. Something similar was also mentioned of the town to which the messengers came, in His saying: ﴿They said, "Indeed, we consider you a bad omen. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you"﴾ [Ya-Sin: 18].

Exalted is He has shown that their ill omen comes from their own disbelief and disobedience, not from the messengers. He said in "al-A'raf": ﴿Unquestionably, their omen is with Allah﴾ [7:131]. He said in Surah "al-Naml" concerning the people of Salih: ﴿He said, "Your omen is with Allah; rather, you are a people being tested"﴾ [An-Naml: 47]. He said in "Ya-Sin": ﴿They said, "Your omen is with you"﴾ [Ya-Sin: 19].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 137:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We caused the people who had been oppressed to inherit the eastern and western parts of the land﴾, the verse.

He does not specify here who these people are, but he stated in surah "al-Shu'ara'" that what is meant by them is the Children of Israel, based on His saying in that same story: ﴿Thus, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit it﴾, the verse [59], and he alluded to this here by His saying after it: ﴿And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel﴾, the verse [al-A'raf: 137].

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel﴾, the verse.

He does not specify here what this good word was that was fulfilled for them, but he explained it in surah al-Qasas by His saying: ﴿And We wished to confer favour upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them the inheritors﴾ and ﴿And We would establish them in the land and show Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers from them that which they feared﴾ [al-Qasas: 5, 6].

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 143:**

(p-40) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "My Lord, show me [Yourself] that I may look at You." He said, "You will not see Me."﴾ — and the rest of the verse.

The Mu'tazilah, who deny that Allah will be seen with the eyes on the Day of Resurrection, have used this verse as evidence for their false doctrine. Yet there are verses indicating that the denial of sight mentioned here applies only to this world, whereas in the Hereafter the believers will see Him, exalted is He, with their eyes. This is affirmed by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 22], and His saying concerning the disbelievers: ﴿No! Indeed, they will be veiled from their Lord that Day﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 15]. For from the implication of its opposite it is understood that the believers will not be veiled from Him, exalted is He.

It has also been established from the Prophet ﷺ that, regarding His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿For those who do good is the best [reward] and an increase﴾ [Yunus: 26], he said: "The best [reward] is Paradise, and the increase is looking at the Noble Face of Allah." This is one of the two opinions concerning His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And with Us is more [than what they ask]﴾ [Qaf: 35]. The hadiths from the Prophet ﷺ are mutawatir that the believers will see their Lord on the Day of Resurrection with their eyes.

The verification of the matter is this: seeing Allah, exalted is He, with the eyes is rationally possible in this world and the Hereafter. Among the greatest proofs of its rational possibility in the abode of this world is Moses' saying: ﴿My Lord, show me [Yourself] that I may look at You﴾ [al-A'raf: 143], for Moses was not unaware of what is possible and what is impossible with respect to Allah, exalted is He. As for the legal ruling, it is permissible and will occur in the Hereafter, as the aforementioned verses indicate and as the authentic hadiths have reached the level of mutawatir concerning it. In this world, however, it is legally prohibited, as this verse of "al-A'raf" indicates, and as the hadith "Indeed you will not see your Lord until you die" indicates, as we have clarified in our book (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 148:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Did they not see that it neither speaks to them nor guides them to a way? They took it, and they were wrongdoers.﴾ In this noble verse He makes clear the feebleness of the minds of the calf-worshippers, and rebukes them for worshipping that which neither speaks to them nor guides them to a way. He clarified this in Surah Ta-Ha with His saying: ﴿Did they not see that it does not return to them any word, and that it possesses for them neither harm nor benefit?﴾ [20:89], and the verse continues. We have already mentioned in Surah al-Baqarah (tafsir, explanation of the Qur'an) that in all the verses about their taking the calf as a god, the second object is omitted throughout the Qur'an, as in His saying here: ﴿And the people of Musa, after him, made from their ornaments a calf, a body with a sound﴾ [7:148], that is, they took it as a god (ilah). We have already mentioned that the purpose (nukta, subtle point) of always omitting it is to alert that it is not fitting to utter that a calf fashioned from inanimate matter is a god. He, exalted is He, has always pointed to this omitted object in Surah Ta-Ha with His saying: ﴿So they said, "This is your god and the god of Musa"﴾ [20:88].

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (*Adwa' al-Bayan*) on surah 7, verse 149:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when they were overcome with regret, and saw that they had indeed gone astray, they said, "If our Lord does not have mercy upon us and forgive us, we will surely be among the losers."﴾.

(p-41) In this noble verse, God, exalted is He, makes clear that the worshippers of the calf acknowledged their sin and regretted what they had done. In surah "al-Baqarah" (The Cow), He stated explicitly their repentance, their acceptance of being killed, and God's, exalted is He, acceptance of their repentance, in His saying: ﴿And [recall] when Moses said to his people, "O my people, indeed you have wronged yourselves by your taking of the calf [for worship], so turn in repentance to your Creator and kill yourselves. That is better for you in the sight of your Creator." And He accepted your repentance. Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful.﴾ [54].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 150:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved, he said, "Evil is what you did after me in my absence. Did you hasten the command of your Lord?"﴾ ...the verse.

Allah clarified what is mentioned here by His saying in Ta-Ha: ﴿He said, "O my people, did your Lord not make you a good promise? Has the time seemed long to you, or did you wish that wrath from your Lord should descend upon you, so you broke your promise to me?" They said, "We did not break our promise to you by our own choice"﴾ ...the verse [al-Tariq: 87].

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And he seized his brother by the head, drawing him toward himself. He said, "Son of my mother, indeed the people have oppressed me"﴾ ...the verse.

In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, refers to what the Prophet of Allah, Harun, offered as his excuse to his brother Musa for the blame that Musa directed at him. Allah clarified it in Ta-Ha by His saying: ﴿He said, "Son of my mother, do not seize my beard or my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say, 'You caused division among the Children of Israel and did not observe my word.'"﴾ [94]. Allah, exalted is He, also explicitly declared his innocence by His saying:

﴿And Harun had already said to them before, "O my people, you are only being tested by it, and indeed your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my command." They said, "We will not cease to be devoted to it until Moses returns to us."﴾ [Ta-Ha: 90].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 158:

Allah's saying: ﴿Say, "O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all."﴾

This noble verse explicitly states that he (ﷺ) is a messenger to all of mankind, and he stated this in many verses, such as:

• His saying: ﴿And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind﴾ [Saba': 28],

• and His saying: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion (al-Furqan) upon His servant that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ [al-Furqan: 1],

• and His saying: ﴿And whoever of the factions disbelieves in it, then the Fire is his promised place﴾ [Hud: 17]. In another place, He restricted the generality of his message to the reaching of this Qur'an, which is His saying: ﴿And this Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whoever it reaches﴾ [al-An'am: 19]. He also explicitly stated that his message includes the People of the Book along with the Arabs,

• by His saying: ﴿And say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered, "Have you submitted?" And if they submit, then they have been guided; but if they turn away, then upon you is only the conveyance [of the message]﴾ [Al 'Imran: 20],

and other verses besides these.

* *

Allah's saying: ﴿So believe in Allah and His Messenger, the unlettered prophet, who believes in Allah and His words﴾, and so on.

He did not specify here the multitude of His words, but He specified that in other places, such as His saying: ﴿Say, "If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord are exhausted, even if We brought the like of it as replenishment."﴾ [al-Kahf: 109], and His saying: ﴿...And if whatever trees upon the earth were pens and the sea [were ink], replenished thereafter by seven seas, the words of Allah would not be exhausted.﴾ [Luqman: 27]

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 169:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Was not the covenant of the Book taken from them, that they would not say about Allah except the truth?﴾ – and the verse continues.

This covenant mentioned here is explained by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [mention] when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Book, [saying], "You must make it clear to the people and not conceal it." But they cast it behind their backs and exchanged it for a small price. And wretched is what they purchase.﴾ [Aal 'Imran: 187].

The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 7, verse 172:

﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, and made them testify concerning themselves: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes, we testify." Lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection: "Indeed we were unaware of this."﴾ ﴿Or lest you should say: "Only our fathers associated others with God before, and we were descendants after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?"﴾

In this noble verse there are two well-known interpretations (wajhan min al-tafsir, "two aspects of tafsir") among the scholars:

The first: the meaning of His taking the descendants of the Children of Adam from their loins is the bringing into existence of one generation after another from them, and the creating of one people after other peoples, as He said: ﴿As He produced you from the descendants of another people﴾ [al-An'am: 133], and He said: ﴿It is He who made you successors upon the earth﴾ [Fatir: 39], and He said: ﴿And makes you successors﴾ [al-Naml: 62], and similar verses. According to this view, the meaning of His words ﴿And made them testify concerning themselves: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes"﴾ [al-A'raf: 172] is that their being made to testify concerning themselves is only through the decisive proofs established for them that He is their Lord, the One deserving of them worshipping Him alone. Accordingly, the meaning of ﴿They said: "Yes"﴾ is: they said that by the tongue of their state (bi-lisan al-hal), because of the manifestness of the proofs. A parallel to the use of "testimony" for the testimony of the tongue of state is His saying: ﴿It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God while bearing witness against themselves of disbelief﴾ [al-Tawbah: 17], i.e., by the tongue of their state, in saying that. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is to his Lord ungrateful﴾ and that ﴿he is, to that, a witness﴾ [al-Adiyat: 6–7], i.e., also by the tongue of his state, in saying that this is what is meant in this verse as well.

Those who held this view argued that God, exalted is He, made this testimony a proof against them for associating others with Him, exalted is He, in His saying: ﴿Lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection: "Indeed we were unaware of this." Or lest you should say: "Only our fathers associated others with God before, and we were descendants after them"﴾ [al-A'raf: 172–173]. They said: if the testimony mentioned were the testimony taken from them on the Day of the Covenant while they were in the form of atoms (dharr), it would not have been a proof against them, (p-43) because none of them remembers it when they exist in this world, and what a person has no knowledge of cannot be a proof against him. If it is said: the report of the Messengers about the mentioned covenant suffices for its establishment, we say:

Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir: "The answer to that is that the polytheist deniers deny all that the Messengers brought them, of this and other things, and this was made an independent proof against them. This indicates that it is the fitrah (innate disposition) upon which they were created, of monotheism. This is why He said: ﴿Lest you should say﴾ and so on." End of his words verbatim.

Having learned this aspect we have mentioned in the interpretation of the verse, and what its proponent cited from the Qur'an for it, know that the other aspect regarding the meaning of the verse is: that God brought forth all the descendants of Adam from the loins of their fathers in the form of atoms, made them testify concerning themselves by the tongue of speech: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ ﴿They said: "Yes"﴾, and then after that He sent Messengers reminding them of that covenant, which all had forgotten, and none of them was born while remembering it. The report of the Messengers about it produces certainty of its existence.

The compiler of this work, may God pardon him, says: this last aspect is supported by the Book and the Sunnah.

As for the manner in which the Qur'an indicates it: the implication of the first view is that the decisive proofs God established for them, such as the creation of the heavens and the earth and the marvels of God's handiwork in them that indicate He is the Lord worshipped alone, and the fitrah He instilled in them upon which He created them, establish the proof against them even if no warner came to them. The Qur'anic verses explicitly state, in great number, that God does not punish anyone until He establishes the proof against him by the warning of the fitrah. Among these is His saying: ﴿And We would never punish until We sent a Messenger﴾ [al-Isra': 15], for He said in it "until We send a Messenger," and did not say "until We create intellects, set up proofs, and instill a fitrah."

Among these also is His saying: ﴿Messengers as bearers of good tidings and warners, so that mankind will have no argument against God after the Messengers﴾ [al-Nisa': 165]. He explicitly stated that what establishes the proof against people and cuts off their excuse is the warning of the Messengers, not the setting up of proofs and creation upon the fitrah.

This proof for which the Messengers were sent to establish he explained in Ta-Ha by His saying: ﴿And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said: "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a Messenger so we could follow Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced?"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 134], and he alluded to it in al-Qasas by His saying: ﴿And if not that a disaster should afflict them for what their hands have put forward, they would say: "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a Messenger so we could follow Your signs and be among the believers?"﴾ [al-Qasas: 47]. Among these is that He, exalted is He, explicitly stated that all the people of the Fire had their excuse cut off in this world by the warning of the Messengers, and did not suffice with the setting up of proofs, as in His saying: ﴿Every time a group is thrown into it, its keepers ask them: "Did there not come to you a warner?" They say: "Yes, a warner had come to us, but we denied and said: God did not send down anything; you are only in great error."﴾ [al-Mulk: 8–9], and His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened and its keepers will say to them: "Did there not come to you Messengers from among you reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?" They will say: "Yes, but the word of punishment has come into effect upon the disbelievers."﴾ [al-Zumar: 71]. It is known that the word "kullama" (every time) in His saying ﴿Every time a group is thrown into it﴾ is a word of generality, and that the word "alladhina" (those who) in His saying ﴿And those who disbelieved﴾ is also a word of generality, since the relative pronoun encompasses everything its clause includes.

As for the Sunnah: many hadiths indicate that God brought forth the descendants of Adam in the form of atoms, and took the covenant from them as mentioned here, and some of them are authentic. Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir of this verse: Abu 'Umar, meaning Ibn 'Abd al-Barr, said: "However, the meaning of this hadith has been authentically related from the Prophet ﷺ through many well-established routes, from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, Abu Hurayrah, and others, may Allah be pleased with them all." End of the portion needed, verbatim.

This disagreement which we have mentioned, whether the obligation of monotheism is established by the setting up of proofs, or whether there must be the sending of Messengers to warn, is the basis of the well-known disagreement among the scholars of usul al-fiqh (principles of jurisprudence) concerning the people of the fatrah (the interval between Messengers): will they enter the Fire because of their disbelief? Al-Qarafi reported a consensus (ijma') on it, and al-Nawawi affirmed it in his Sharh Muslim. Or will they be excused because of the fatrah, which is the apparent meaning of the verses we have cited? To this disagreement he alluded in Maraqi al-Su'ud with his words:

"The one in the fatrah is not considered in the branches (furu'), but among the usul scholars there is dispute among them."

We have verified this question, along with discussing the evidences of both sides, in our book (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab) in Surah "Bani Isra'il," in discussing His saying: ﴿And We would never punish until We send a Messenger﴾, and for that reason we have abridged it here.

This is the commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 176:

His Exalted Words: ﴿So his likeness is like that of the dog: if you chase it, it pants, or if you leave it, it pants﴾, etc.

Allah, exalted is He, struck the parable (mathal, a likeness or illustrative example) for this lowly one to whom He gave His signs but who then withdrew from them, with the dog. The baseness of the dog did not prevent Allah, exalted is He, from using it as a parable. Likewise, He struck the parable with the fly in His words: ﴿O mankind, a parable has been presented, so listen to it. Indeed, those you invoke other than Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it. And if the fly should snatch away from them a thing, they could not recover it from him. Weak are the pursuer and pursued﴾ [al-Hajj: 73]. Likewise, He struck the parable with the spider's house in His words: ﴿The example of those who take allies other than Allah is like the spider who makes for herself a home. And indeed, the weakest of homes is the spider's home, if only they knew﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 41]. Likewise, He struck the parable with the donkey in His words: ﴿The example of those who were entrusted with the Torah but did not carry it is like the example of a donkey who carries volumes. Wretched is the example of the people who deny the signs of Allah. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 5].

These verses indicate that He, exalted is He, is not shy about explaining sublime knowledge through parables drawn from humble things. He has stated this meaning explicitly in His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to present an example, [even] of a mosquito or what is above it﴾.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 180:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And leave those who distort (yulhidūn) regarding His names; they will be recompensed for what they used to do.﴾

In this verse, Allah, exalted is He, threatens those who distort (yulhidūn) regarding His names with two threats.

The first: the imperative form in His saying "wadharū" (leave), for it is for threatening.

The second: in His saying, ﴿they will be recompensed for what they used to do﴾. In the surah of Ḥā Mīm "as-Sajdah," He threatened those who distort His verses with the fact that they are not hidden from Him, in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who distort Our verses are not hidden from Us﴾ [41:40]. Then He followed that with His saying: ﴿Is he who is thrown into the Fire better, or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection?﴾, and so on.

The original meaning of ilḥād (distortion, deviation; lit. inclining) in the language is "al-maylu" (inclination), and from it comes al-laḥd (the niche dug in the side of a grave). The meaning of their distortion regarding His names is what is found in their deriving the name "al-Lāt" from the name "Allāh," the name "al-ʿUzzā" from the name "al-ʿAzīz," the name "Manāt" from "al-Mannān," and the like. The Arabs say "laḥada" and "alḥada" with one meaning, and both readings are based on this: yulḥidūn with the yā' and ḥā' vowelled with fatḥ in the first, and with ḍammah and kasrah on the ḥā' in the second.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 187:**

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None will reveal it at its time except Him.﴾ (the verse)

This noble verse indicates that the time of the Hour's establishment is known only to Allah, Majestic and Exalted. Other verses also indicate this, such as His saying: ﴿They ask you about the Hour, when will it occur?﴾ ﴿In what are you concerned with mentioning it?﴾ ﴿To your Lord is its finality.﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 42, 43, 44]; and His saying: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him.﴾ [al-An'am: 59]. It is also established in the Sahih (the authentic collection of hadith) from him (ﷺ) that these are the five things mentioned in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour﴾ (the verse) [Luqman: 34].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 188:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And had I known the unseen, I would have acquired much of the good﴾.

This verse indicates that he (ﷺ) did not know of the unseen except what Allah taught him. Allah, exalted is He, had commanded him to say that he does not know the unseen, in His saying in "al-An'am": ﴿Say, "I do not tell you that with me are the treasuries of Allah, nor do I know the unseen"﴾ (p-46) [50]. He also said: ﴿[He is] Knower of the unseen, and He does not disclose His unseen to anyone, except to one whom He has approved of the messengers﴾ [al-Jinn: 26-27], and He said: ﴿Say, "None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah"﴾ [an-Naml: 65], along with other verses.

As for the meaning of "the good" (al-khayr) in this noble verse, it has been said that it means wealth. This is supported by the frequent occurrence of "khayr" in the sense of wealth in the Qur'an, such as:

• His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, he is intense in his love of wealth﴾ [al-'Adiyat: 8],

• His saying: ﴿if he leaves behind wealth﴾ [al-Baqarah: 180],

• His saying: ﴿Say, "Whatever wealth you spend..."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 215],

along with other verses.

It has also been said that the meaning of "the good" here is righteous deeds, as Mujahid and others said. The first view is the correct one, because he (ﷺ) acquired greatly of the good, which is righteous deeds, since his deeds were constant; and in one narration, when he did a deed, he would make it firm (persistent).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 189:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He made from it its mate, that he might find tranquility in her﴾ — the verse.

In this noble verse He mentions that He created Hawwa' (Eve) from Adam so that he would find tranquility in her, i.e., that he would be at ease with her and content in her company. In another place He makes clear that He made the spouses of his offspring likewise, namely in His saying: ﴿And among His signs is that He created for you mates from among yourselves that you may find tranquility in them, and He placed between you affection and mercy﴾ [al-Rum: 21].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 7, verse 190:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when He gave them a righteous child, they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them. But exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him.﴾

There are two well-known interpretations of this noble verse among the scholars, and the Qur'an supports one of them.

The first: Hawwa' (Eve) had children who would not survive. She became pregnant, and Satan came to her and said: "Name this child 'Abd al-Harith (Servant of al-Harith), for he will survive." Al-Harith is one of the names of Satan. So she named him 'Abd al-Harith. Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So when He gave them a righteous child﴾ [al-A'raf: 190], meaning a righteous male human child, "they attributed to Him partners" by naming him 'Abd al-Harith. A hadith marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ) has come with something similar to this, but it is ma'lul (defective), as Ibn Kathir clarified in his tafsir.

The second: The meaning of the verse is that when He gave Adam and Hawwa' a righteous child, many of their descendants later disbelieved in Him. The act of the descendants is attributed to Adam and Hawwa' because they are the origin of their descendants, as He said: ﴿And We created you, then We fashioned you﴾ [al-A'raf: 11], meaning by Our fashioning of your father Adam, because he is their origin, as evidenced by His saying after it: ﴿Then We said to the angels: Prostrate to Adam﴾. This last interpretation is also supported by His saying, exalted is He, after it: (p-47) ﴿But exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him﴾ ﴿Do they associate with Him that which creates nothing and is itself created?﴾ [al-A'raf: 190, 191]. This is a clear Qur'anic text that the intended ones are the polytheists from the children of Adam, not Adam and Hawwa'. Many have preferred this interpretation because of the Qur'an's indication of it, and among those who held it is al-Hasan al-Basri, and Ibn Kathir preferred it. And Allah knows best.

**The commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah al-A'raf, verse 199:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Hold to forgiveness, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant.﴾ ﴿And if a prompting from Satan should stir you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.﴾

In this noble verse, He clarified how the ignorant among the devils of mankind and the jinn should be treated. He explained that the devil of mankind is to be dealt with gently, by taking forgiveness, turning away from his ignorance and his evil. As for the devil of the jinn, there is no escape from him except by seeking refuge in Allah from him. He said of the first: ﴿Hold to forgiveness, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant﴾ [al-A'raf: 199], and He said of the second: ﴿And if a prompting from Satan should stir you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ [al-A'raf: 200]. He clarified what we have mentioned in two other places.

The first: in Surah ﴿Indeed, the believers have succeeded﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 1]. He said in it, concerning the devil of mankind: ﴿Repel evil with that which is better; We are most knowing of what they describe﴾ [96], and He said in the other: ﴿And say, "My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the evil suggestions of the devils, and I seek refuge in You, my Lord, lest they be present with me"﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 97-98] [as printed].

The second: in Ha Mim "al-Sajdah." He said in it, concerning the devil of mankind: ﴿And not equal are the good deed and the bad. Repel evil with that which is better, and thereupon the one whom between you and him is enmity will become as though he were a devoted friend﴾ [Fussilat: 34]. And He added here that this is not granted to all people; rather, Allah grants it only to one who has great fortune and great blessing with Him. So He said: ﴿But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune﴾ [Fussilat: 35]. Then He said, concerning the devil of the jinn: ﴿And if a prompting from Satan should stir you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ [Fussilat: 36].

The Exalted's statement: ﴿And their brothers extend them in error, then they do not hold back﴾.

In this noble verse He mentions that the brothers of mankind among the devils extend mankind in error, and then they do not hold back. He also explains this in other places, such as His saying: ﴿Have you not seen that We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers, inciting them with incitement?﴾ [Maryam: 83], and His saying: ﴿O assembly of jinn, you have taken much from mankind﴾ [al-An'am: 128]. In another place He explains that some of mankind are brothers of the devils, which is His saying: ﴿Indeed, the squanderers were brothers of the devils﴾ [al-Isra': 27], and the verse continues.
